        continue()
    endif()
    # run mg15 lane MP1: THE DS SLEEP/WAKE PAIR AND ITS SCHEDULER.
    # src/OS_SleepThread.c's first act is data_020a612c->node, and
    # hal/cxx_aliases.cpp hosts data_020a612c as zero -- so the ROM body is a
    # null dereference on its first call, and port/nfs_names_map.txt:402 has
    # said so since the NitroFS seat. MEASURED by build target
    # mp_sleepwake_rom: 0xC0000005, through the real veneer. It is not
    # theoretical either -- src/func_02018e68.c (slice_mg1) reaches it on the
    # file-read failure path, so today the error report faults before it can
    # print. Past the deref, src/func_02057f54.c reschedules through
    # ARMProcessorMode/ARMSaveContext/ARMRestoreContext, none of which has a
    # host body and none of which has an honest one to write.
    # hal/os_thread.cpp reproduces the queue-word half of the contract exactly
    # and replaces the ARM context switch with a bounded host pump. It is
    # appended through SLICE_COMMS_SOURCES below, which every consumer of
    # SLICE10_CAM_SOURCES also takes -- checked: the three add_executable
    # lines that use this variable are the three that use that one.
    if(src MATCHES "/OS_SleepThread\\.c$"
       OR src MATCHES "/OS_WakeupThread\\.c$"
       OR src MATCHES "/func_02057f54\\.c$")
        continue()
    endif()
    list(APPEND SLICE10_CAM_SOURCES "${src}")
endforeach()

# what keeps the port portable back to hardware. The transport contract a

# in src/func_0203ea5c.c's own order, because that TU is still in no slice and

# SLICE36_SOURCES IS INERT. It is parsed here and added to NO target, so these
# 33 lines compile nothing and link nothing. The comment that stood here said
# "Linked but NOT yet called", which was false in its first half: nothing is
# linked. The list is kept because it is the gate's inventory and because the
# measurement below is worth having written down, not because it is wired.
#
# WHY IT STAYS THAT WAY, measured in wave 4 rather than argued. Adding
# ${SLICE36_SOURCES} to walk_window and building fails the link with 43
# distinct unresolved externals and ZERO duplicate definitions -- so the
# blocker is not a clash with the host boot, it is that the slice does not
# close. The 43 sort into three groups and none of them is a line in a file:
#
#   22  storage the port hosts nowhere: data_020755e0/5f0/600/6f0/720/769/76a,
#       data_0208ecf4, data_0208ee00, data_02092130, data_02092778,
#       data_0209d4a8, data_0209f278, data_0209f290, data_0209f300,
#       data_0209f304, data_020758c8, data_020a0f04, data_ov001_020ad620,
#       data_ov001_020ad624, _ZTV9FaderWipe, and LoadOrUnloadObjectOverlays
#   15  matched TUs that exist in src/ and are not on this slice at all:
#       GetControllerMode, LoadOverlay, _ZN10FaderColorD2Ev, the five GX::SetBankFor*
#       setters, func_02018908, func_02018934, func_020190b8, func_02023408,
#       func_0203d81c, func_02053e1c, func_02053e34
#    6  ON THIS SLICE ALREADY and still unresolved: _Z17LoadLevelOverlaysi,
#       ShadowModel::CleanAll, Stage::LoadGraphics2D, Stage::LoadFog,
#       Stage::LoadTextureTransformers, FaderWipe::LoadAndSetFile
#
# That last group is what decides it. Those six .cpp files define the real C++
# METHOD -- src/_ZN5Stage7LoadFogEv.cpp compiles `void Stage::LoadFog()`, which
# MSVC mangles ?LoadFog@Stage@@... -- while Stage::InitResources calls the
# ROM's C name __ZN5Stage7LoadFogEv. Listing the file does not produce the
# symbol its caller wants; a hand-written face does, the way
# hal/method_faces.cpp already carries its own. So the slice head's "all 45
# direct callees are matched, nothing here is written by hand, this slice is
# the wiring" does not survive a build: six faces have to be written, 22
# globals hosted and 15 more callees enrolled before the boot swap it describes
# is reachable at all. Wiring it in today only breaks the build, which is why
# the honest move is to leave it inert and say so.
#
# ShadowModel::CleanAll is the one line here that IS doing work today, and it
# does it from slice_w1l3.txt instead -- see the block in that file.
port_read_lines("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/slice_gate36.txt" SLICE36_LINES)
set(SLICE36_SOURCES "")
foreach(line IN LISTS SLICE36_LINES)
    string(STRIP "${line}" line)
    if(line MATCHES "^#" OR line STREQUAL "")
        continue()
    endif()
    list(APPEND SLICE36_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../${line}")
endforeach()

# Stage 4, lane SD0: gate 36 WIRED, which is what the block above says nobody
# had done. port/slice_s4_slot0.txt is SLICE36_SOURCES minus src/LoadArchive.c
# (the one real LNK2005, against hal/scene_boot.cpp's PORT_HOST_ABI host body),
# minus src/UnloadArchive.c and src/_Z17LoadLevelOverlaysi.cpp (host bodies in
# hal/stage_slot0.cpp instead), plus the three matched callees the closure
# names and no active slice carries.
#
# THE 43 THE BLOCK ABOVE MEASURED IS NOW ZERO, and none of the three groups it
# sorted them into survived as written:
#   the 22 unhosted globals   six are romdata rows (data_020755e0/5f0/600,
#       data_02092778 and the two 0x9a sound columns), one is
#       hal/ptr_tables.cpp table 4 (data_020756f0, twelve ov002 pointers), one
#       is an /alternatename (data_02075720 onto VS_STAR_SPAWN_ORDERS), two are
#       4-byte BSS words in hal/stage_slot0.cpp, and the rest closed on their
#       own as the port grew -- data_0208ecf4 and LoadOrUnloadObjectOverlays
#       through hal/scene_boot.cpp, _ZTV9FaderWipe and the two ov001 words
#       through lane SL0.
#   the 15 unsliced callees   twelve closed as other slices took them; three
#       are on this slice.
#   the 6 already-on-the-slice  five are C-name faces (four in
#       hal/stage_slot0.cpp, FaderWipe::LoadAndSetFile in hal/fader_wipes.cpp),
#       and _Z17LoadLevelOverlaysi is a host body.
# The block above is kept as written because the measurement in it is the
# reason this one could be short.
port_read_lines("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/slice_s4_slot0.txt" SLICE_S4_SLOT0_LINES)
set(SLICE_S4_SLOT0_SOURCES ${SCN3D_HOSTGEN_GEN})

# gate 70: func_ov084_0212f460 is C++ inside a .c (the gate-9 case) -- it opens
# an `extern "C"` block MSVC's C front end will not parse -- so it goes through
# hostgen, which re-emits it as .cpp with the symbols wrapped back to C linkage.
# (func_ov084_0212f33c uses a C99 compound literal MSVC warns on as C4576; that
# is suppressed per target below rather than transformed.)
# EMPTIED 2026-09-13 (lane SYNC3). main folded func_ov084_0212f460 into
# src/actors/daPkn_c.cpp, a .cpp TU, so the C-linkage wrap hostgen gave the .c
# source is what the TU already is. That TU is also QUARANTINED out of every
# slice (its func_ov084_0212f204 calls ClosestPlayer with no receiver), so the
# body is out of the link either way and a generated copy would only put the
# receiver-less call back.
set(GATE_L7_SYMS)
set(GATE_L7_GEN "")
foreach(sym IN LISTS GATE_L7_SYMS)
    if(EXISTS "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/${sym}.c")
        set(sym_src "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/${sym}.c")
    else()
        set(sym_src "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/${sym}.cpp")
    endif()
    set(sym_out "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src/src/${sym}.cpp")
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT "${sym_out}"
        COMMAND python "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/hostgen.py"
                --out "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src" ${sym}
        DEPENDS "${sym_src}" "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/hostgen.py"
        COMMENT "hostgen ${sym}")
    list(APPEND GATE_L7_GEN "${sym_out}")
endforeach()

# Two MR_I_PROJECTILE TUs need hostgen, both mwcc-vs-MSVC syntax quirks the
# byte-verified tree must not be edited for (the gate-32 / gate-64 treatment).
# _ZN8daEyBm_c18SpawnDestroyEffectEv is C++ inside a .c -- `struct Callback {}`, an empty
# struct, which MSVC will not compile as C (C2016); hostgen emits it as .cpp
# with the symbols wrapped back to C linkage.
# _ZN8daEyBm_c10HurtPlayerEv is the decl_common.h HEADER_SHADOW case: that header
# declares it `(void*)` inside its extern "C" block while the TU defines it
# `(char*)` -- one register on the ROM, C2733 to MSVC. This lane adds the
# HEADER_SHADOW table entry in tools/hostgen.py.
# EMPTIED 2026-09-13 (lane SYNC3). main folded both into
# src/game/actors/d_a_ey_bm.cpp and made them real C++ METHODS of daEyBm_c
# rather than extern "C" free functions. The empty-struct-in-a-.c case went with
# the .c, and HurtPlayer's C2733 went with the free function: that TU does not
# include decl_common.h, so the header's declaration of the old C-linkage name
# meets nothing.
set(GATE_W7B_SYMS)
set(GATE_W7B_GEN "")
foreach(sym IN LISTS GATE_W7B_SYMS)
    if(EXISTS "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/${sym}.c")
        set(sym_src "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/${sym}.c")
    else()
        set(sym_src "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/${sym}.cpp")
    endif()
    set(sym_out "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src/src/${sym}.cpp")
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT "${sym_out}"
        COMMAND python "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/hostgen.py"
                --out "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src" ${sym}
        DEPENDS "${sym_src}" "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/hostgen.py"
        COMMENT "hostgen ${sym}")
    list(APPEND GATE_W7B_GEN "${sym_out}")
endforeach()

# The rock's Behavior is the only TU in the tree that spells seven arm9/ov002
# functions by recovered friendly names that exist nowhere in the binary. Each
# target is pinned by the reloc out of that body's own range (ov080 relocs,
# Behavior = 0x0212459c..0x0212478c) and named from config/arm9/symbols.txt,
# never from the friendly name. A -D and not /alternatename directives on
# purpose: these are single global names of the G0/G1 kind, and an alias LHS
# another overlay's recovery pass reuses for a different address would
# misroute silently the day that overlay lands. A -D cannot be defeated.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/_ZN13MontyMoleRock8BehaviorEv.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "Actor_MakeVanishLuigiWork=_ZN8dActor_c19MakeVanishLuigiWorkER5dCc_c;Actor_FindWithID=_ZN8dActor_c10FindWithIDEj;Player_Hurt=_ZN6Player4HurtERK7Vector3j5Fix12IiEjjj;Actor_UpdatePos=_ZN8dActor_c9UpdatePosEP5dCc_c;Enemy_UpdateWMClsn=_ZN12dEnemyBase_c12UpdateWMClsnER10dBgCh_Actrj;CylinderClsn_Clear=_ZN5dCc_c5ClearEv;CylinderClsn_Update=_ZN5dCc_c6UpdateEv")

# and 0x02123c28 both module:overlay(78), unambiguous -- and dsd named that
# same address for ov080 too, so their C spells it with the rock's destructor
# name. Without this they would have called the rock's destructor.
# tools/alternatename_guard.py failed the build the first time the seat linked;
# the dead directive is deleted there and the routing lands here, where a -D
# cannot be defeated.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/actors/daBombking_c.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/actors/daBombking_c.cpp"
    # and the generated copy, lane DUPES: this TU is on PORT_HOSTGEN_TU
    # now, so the raw path alone would set the property on a source

    "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src/src/actors/daBombking_c.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src/src/actors/daBombking_c.cpp"

# TRAP 1, and it is the live one. src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km1_ukishima.cpp (id 135's

# body would have released the game heap pointer -- the CannonHatch/MetalNet
# shape, the PATH_LIFT case exactly. The two targets are read off this body's
# own literal pool: 0x02111278 -> 0x021125e8 and 0x0211127c -> 0x021125e0,
# both module:overlay(43), each feeding a SharedFilePtr::Release at 0x02111260
# and 0x02111268. The rename goes to private names this lane owns, not
# straight to the mount names, because include/decl_common.h:396 declares
# `extern int G1[];` and MSVC rejects the redeclaration; the two private names
# bind onto the mounted cells in hal/actor_classes_ov043.cpp.
# src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km1_ukishima.cpp IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. Its G0 is a DIFFERENT
# object -- the game heap it hands Memory::Deallocate, literal at 0x02111238
# relocating to 0x020a0eac module:main -- which is what cxx_aliases.cpp already
# binds. Renaming it would break a binding that is right today.
# lane CDEFS 2026-09-16: a dead COMPILE_DEFINITIONS row stood here.
# A LATER set_source_files_properties() names d_a_obj_km1_ukishima.cpp for the same
# property, and that call REPLACES this one, so nothing on this row ever
# reached the compiler. Each definition it carried, against the synced TU:
#   G0=port_ov043_ukishima_file0  --  dead, the TU does not spell G0
#   G1=port_ov043_ukishima_file1  --  dead, the TU does not spell G1
# Deleted rather than merged. The surviving row is unchanged.
# TRAP 3: src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km1_ukishima.cpp (InitResources) spells ov043's own two bss
# cells with ov047 names. ov043 and ov047 are distinct objects sharing the load
# window and dsd raced the name; the load sites are the same two addresses the
# sinit initialises, both module:overlay(43). Neither ov047 name resolves in
# port/ today, so this is a hard link error rather than a silent miscall. Safe
# as a straight -D to the mount names: decl_common.h declares
# data_ov047_021125e0/e8 as `extern int [];` and declares no data_ov043_
# 021125e0/e8 at all, so there is nothing to conflict with.
# lane CDEFS 2026-09-16: a dead COMPILE_DEFINITIONS row stood here.
# A LATER set_source_files_properties() names d_a_obj_km1_ukishima.cpp for the same
# property, and that call REPLACES this one, so nothing on this row ever
# reached the compiler. Each definition it carried, against the synced TU:
#   data_ov047_021125e8=data_ov043_021125e8  --  dead, the TU does not spell data_ov047_021125e8
#   data_ov047_021125e0=data_ov043_021125e0  --  dead, the TU does not spell data_ov047_021125e0
# Deleted rather than merged. The surviving row is unchanged.
# TRAP 4: src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km1_ukishima.cpp (the deleting destructor) writes VT0 then
# VT1 and both are placeholders. Its own literal pool names them:
# 0x02111230 -> 0x021122b8 module:overlay(43), the class's own table, which is
# the host array; 0x02111234 -> 0x0210ae38 module:overlay(2), the Platform base
# table, which hal/actor_classes.cpp:583 already defines and fills. Renamed to

# src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km1_ukishima.cpp (the D1) writes the SAME pair BY NAME and needs no

# ---- lane cast-ov026: the per-source renames -------------------------------
#
# A. THE SHARED ROLE-NAME PLACEHOLDERS. A comment-stripped sweep of all 54
# ov026 TUs for VT/VT0/VT1/VT2/G0/G1/G2/R0/R1/R2/HEAP returns exactly five
# files. hal/cxx_aliases.cpp binds bare G0 -> data_020a0eac (the GAME HEAP) and
# bare G1 -> data_ov002_0210e05c (SignPost's KCL) for the whole link, so an
# unrenamed placeholder here does not fail a link -- it releases the wrong
# storage, the CannonHatch/MetalNet/PathLift shape. Every target below is the
# address that TU's OWN ROM body loads, read out of the literal pool of
# extracted/overlays/overlay_0026.bin:
#
#   _ZN17daObjWlPolelift_cD0Ev (89's D0)   pool 0211122c/1230: VT0=0x02113ae0, G0=0x020a0eac
#   _ZN13BowserShutterD0Ev (91's D0)   pool 02111758/5c/60: VT0=0x02113ba4,
#                                     VT1=0x0210ae38 (_ZTV10dBgActor_c), G0=0x020a0eac
#   _ZN13BowserShutter16CleanupResourcesEv (91 Cleanup) pool 021117a0/a4: G0=0x02113ebc, G1=0x02113eb4
#   _ZN9SubmarineD0Ev (90's D0)   pool 02111948/4c/50: VT0=0x02113c6c,
#                                     VT1=0x0210ae38, G0=0x020a0eac
#   _ZN9Submarine16CleanupResourcesEv (90 Cleanup) pool 02111990/94: G0=0x02113ee4, G1=0x02113edc
#
# VT0 goes to the HOST ARRAY in each case (all five vtables are excluded from
# the mount). VT1 is spelled _ZTV10dBgActor_c to match what the sibling D1s
# (_ZN13BowserShutterD1Ev.c, _ZN9SubmarineD1Ev.c) already write BY NAME;
# hal/actor_classes.cpp:591 defines that array and dual-fills it with
# _ZTV10dBgActor_c.
# The four SharedFilePtr targets and the polelift's collision vector go through
# PRIVATE NAMES this lane owns, bound in hal/actor_classes_ov026.cpp with a
# C-name /alternatename, because include/decl_common.h already declares
# data_ov026_02113ebc/eb4/edc/ee4 as `char[]` and data_ov026_02113a9c as
# `Vector3` while the TUs declare their placeholders as `extern int G0[];` and
# a local `struct V3` -- a direct -D is the C2371/C2372 redeclaration the ov006
# Mg3DEsp block measured. Each private LHS is undefined everywhere else, so
# those aliases cannot be defeated.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/_ZN17daObjWlPolelift_cD0Ev.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "VT0=_ZTV17daObjWlPolelift_c;G0=data_020a0eac")
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/_ZN13BowserShutterD0Ev.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "VT0=_ZTV21daObjWlKoopaShutter_c;VT1=_ZTV10dBgActor_c;G0=data_020a0eac")
set_source_files_properties(

#
# B. THE SECOND SPELLING OF A HOST-ARRAY VTABLE. Three of the five tables are
# reached under two names by ov026's own sources, and only one host array can
# exist per table because the object's vptr is one word. A -D rather than an
# /alternatename on purpose: a -D cannot be defeated by a later mount (the
# ov071/ov073 R3 failure), and the R5 precedent points the rename AT the host
# array for exactly this case.
#   daObjWlKoopaShutter_c_classInit.c writes _ZTV13BowserShutter, its D1 writes
#     _ZTV21daObjWlKoopaShutter_c -- same address 0x02113ba4.
#   daObjWlSubmarine_c_classInit.c writes _ZTV9Submarine, its D1 writes
#     _ZTV18daObjWlSubmarine_c -- same address 0x02113c6c.
#   _ZN9WhirlpoolD1Ev.c and daWater_Tatumaki_c_classInit.c write _ZTV9Submarine, the D0
#     writes _ZTV18daWater_Tatumaki_c -- same address 0x02113d54, and the
#     _ZTV9Submarine row is the WRONG label (that table's own vtable[-1]
#     typeinfo name string reads 18daWater_Tatumaki_c), so the rename runs
#     toward the right name.
#   _ZN12WaterSuctionD0Ev.c writes _ZTV17daWater_Suikomi_c, the D1 and the
#     Spawn write _ZTV12WaterSuction -- same address 0x02113e24, and here BOTH
#     labels are correct spellings of one class, so the rename is only picking
#     the majority spelling.
# include/decl_common.h declares every one of these as `extern int NAME[];`, so
# each rename produces a duplicate IDENTICAL declaration, which is legal.
set_source_files_properties(

    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS

    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "_ZTV9Submarine=_ZTV18daWater_Tatumaki_c")

    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/_ZN12WaterSuctionD0Ev.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "_ZTV17daWater_Suikomi_c=_ZTV12WaterSuction")
#
# C. THE WRONG-OVERLAY CROSSINGS. ov026 shares the level load window at
# 0x021111a0 with ov014/ov015/ov016/ov020/ov021/ov022/ov029/ov032/ov034/ov036/
# ov045/ov053 and dsd raced the name on four references inside ov026's own
# sources. Each target is ov026's own symbol at the identical address.
#
#   src/func_ov026_021122b0.c calls __sinit_ov045_02112280 where ov026's own
#   func_ov026_02112280 (0x02112280, kind:function, size 0x30) is meant. THIS
#   ONE IS A LIVE HAZARD, not a synonym: ___sinit_ov045_02112280 is ALREADY
#   DEFINED in walk_window by ov013_syms.c.obj (measured in the 0.2.15 baseline
#   map, 0004:000cc184) -- a mounted DATA object at the shared address. Left
#   alone, WaterSuction's state-0 tick would have called into mounted data, and
#   an /alternatename would have been defeated silently. A -D cannot be.
#
#   src/__sinit_ov026_02112d68.c writes data_ov036_02113f58 where ov026's own
#   bss cell data_ov026_02113f58 is meant -- that sinit is ov026's own .init
#   code and the cell it builds is the one WaterSuction::InitResources passes to
#   func_ov026_021122d4. ov036's 0x02113f58 is a real .data symbol of ov036's,
#   which is exactly why this must not be an alias.
#
#   src/_ZN17daObjWlPolelift_c13InitResourcesEv.cpp reads data_ov032_02113a9c (ov026's own
#   0x02113a9c, the polelift's collision half-extents) and calls
#   func_ov053_021112a4 (ov026's own func_ov026_021112a4, the matrix/scale
#   helper immediately above it in the same class block). The first goes
#   through the private name in block A because decl_common.h's own
#   data_ov026_02113a9c declaration would collide; the second is renamed
#   directly -- decl_common.h:1566 declares func_ov053_021112a4 and does not
#   declare func_ov026_021112a4, so there is nothing to conflict with.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/func_ov026_021122b0.c"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "__sinit_ov045_02112280=func_ov026_02112280")
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/__sinit_ov026_02112d68.c"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "data_ov036_02113f58=data_ov026_02113f58")
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/_ZN17daObjWlPolelift_c13InitResourcesEv.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "data_ov032_02113a9c=port_ov026_polelift_clsn;func_ov053_021112a4=func_ov026_021112a4")

# THE SIX PER-SOURCE RENAMES, and where each target came from. Six of the eight
# intermediate destructors are shared-header recoveries: they spell the class's
# OWN table as _ZTV10dBgActor_c and the base it overwrites it with as VT1, and
# hal/cxx_aliases.cpp binds a bare VT1 to auto_bss's dummy for the whole link
# -- so leaving one unrenamed does not fail the link, it writes the wrong table
# into a live object's vptr (the CannonHatch/MetalNet shape). Each target below
# is the address that TU's OWN ROM body loads, read out of the relocations
# INSIDE the function's span in config/arm9/overlays/ov002/relocs.txt:
#
#   _ZN16daObjKaitendai_cD1Ev (D1)  pool 020b66a0/a4:  0x021091d4, 0x0210ae38
#   _ZN16daObjKaitendai_cD0Ev (D0)  pool 020b6658/5c/60: 0x021091d4, 0x0210ae38, 0x020a0eac
#   _ZN13daObjKuruma_cD1Ev (D1)  pool 020b68a8/ac:  0x02109278, 0x0210ae38
#   _ZN13daObjKuruma_cD0Ev (D0)  pool 020b6860/64/68: 0x02109278, 0x0210ae38, 0x020a0eac
#   _ZN17daObjKurumajiku_cD1Ev (D1)  pool 020b6a78/7c:  0x02109320, 0x0210ae38
#   _ZN17daObjKurumajiku_cD0Ev (D0)  pool 020b6a30/34/38: 0x02109320, 0x0210ae38, 0x020a0eac
#
# 0x0210ae38 is _ZTV10dBgActor_c by config/arm9/overlays/ov002/symbols.txt:2225,
# hosted as `void *_ZTV10dBgActor_c[32]` in hal/actor_vtables.cpp; 0x020a0eac is
# the game heap word. The daObjDorifu_c pair (020b4af8 / 020b4a70) and the four
# ov064 bodies spell every one of their targets by its real name and take no -D
# at all, which is why they are not listed here.
foreach(g216 _ZN16daObjKaitendai_cD1Ev _ZN13daObjKuruma_cD1Ev _ZN17daObjKurumajiku_cD1Ev)
    if(g216 STREQUAL "_ZN16daObjKaitendai_cD1Ev")
        set(G216_OWN _ZTV16daObjKaitendai_c)
    elseif(g216 STREQUAL "_ZN13daObjKuruma_cD1Ev")
        set(G216_OWN _ZTV13daObjKuruma_c)
    else()
        set(G216_OWN _ZTV17daObjKurumajiku_c)
    endif()
    set_source_files_properties(
        "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/${g216}.c"
        PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
        "_ZTV10dBgActor_c=${G216_OWN};VT1=_ZTV10dBgActor_c")
endforeach()
foreach(g216 _ZN16daObjKaitendai_cD0Ev _ZN13daObjKuruma_cD0Ev _ZN17daObjKurumajiku_cD0Ev)
    if(g216 STREQUAL "_ZN16daObjKaitendai_cD0Ev")
        set(G216_OWN _ZTV16daObjKaitendai_c)
    elseif(g216 STREQUAL "_ZN13daObjKuruma_cD0Ev")
        set(G216_OWN _ZTV13daObjKuruma_c)
    else()
        set(G216_OWN _ZTV17daObjKurumajiku_c)
    endif()
    set_source_files_properties(
        "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/${g216}.c"
        PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
        "_ZTV10dBgActor_c=${G216_OWN};VT1=_ZTV10dBgActor_c;G0=data_020a0eac")
endforeach()
# THE THREE LIVE-CLASS D1 RENAMES. Same rule, different placeholder names: each
# of these three bodies spells its OWN table by a config RTTI name the port
# hosts under an address name, and the base it overwrites it with as
# _ZTV10dBgActor_c. Targets read out of the relocations inside each function's
# span, not from the recovery's names:
#
#   _ZN16daObjC0_Switch_cD1Ev  0x021111dc -> ov012 0x02112344   0x021111e0 -> 0x0210ae38
#   _ZN10RockPillarD1Ev  0x02112a3c -> ov016 0x02114b00   0x02112a40 -> 0x0210ae38
#   _ZN7SkiLiftD1Ev  0x021111dc -> ov018 0x021138cc   0x021111e0 -> 0x0210ae38
#
# _ZN18daObjClockHuriko_cD1Ev and _ZN4DoorD1Ev spell every word they store by a
# name the port already defines, so they take no -D and are deliberately absent
# here. _ZN13daObjKi_Ita_cD1Ev is not in the gate at all: its MIDDLE store is ov002
# 0x02108fdc, and that intermediate base table is hosted nowhere in this port --
# a table to host, not a rename.
# lane CDEFS 2026-09-16: a dead COMPILE_DEFINITIONS row stood here.
# A LATER set_source_files_properties() names d_a_obj_c0_switch.cpp for the same
# property, and that call REPLACES this one, so nothing on this row ever
# reached the compiler. Each definition it carried, against the synced TU:
#   _ZTV16daObjC0_Switch_c=_ZTV16daObjC0_Switch_c  --  identity rename, a no-op even if it had run
#   _ZTV10dBgActor_c=_ZTV10dBgActor_c  --  identity rename, a no-op even if it had run
# Deleted rather than merged. The surviving row is unchanged.

    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/_ZN10RockPillarD1Ev.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS

    "_ZTV14daObjSm_Lift_c=_ZTV7SkiLift;_ZTV10dBgActor_c=_ZTV10dBgActor_c")
# ---- gate 214 (run link100, lane BOOT): THE ROM'S OWN BOOT CHAIN ------------
#
# The port boots through tests/walk_window.cpp's main(), which stands in for
# the ROM's Entry and main(). Two of the ROM's boot steps were already on that
# path and named as such -- Heap::InitializeRootHeap and
# Heap::InitializeGameHeap(0x3b000, 0) -- and the rest of the chain was not
# there at all, which is why 503 matched translation units reachable ONLY
# through Entry/main were unlinked. hal/boot_os.cpp transcribes the runnable
# spans of src/func_02019780.c, src/main.c and src/func_0201a054.c and calls
# the ROM's own bodies at the points the ROM calls them; everything in this
# slice is reached from there by the ROM's own call graph, never by a call
# added to make a file link.
#
# hal/boot_hw.cpp is the OTHER half and does NOT raise the count: the ARM
# primitives at the leaves of that chain (CP15 cache/MPU, CPSR mode toggles,
# `swp`, the literal-pool veneers, MSL's hand-written format DFA). Each one
# carries a PORT_HOST_ABI: tag naming the instruction MSVC cannot assemble, so
# port/tools/linkage.py counts them as documented exceptions rather than as
# work still owed.
#
# WHAT IS NOT IN HERE, and it is hardware and not effort: the four PXI arms of
# func_02058c84 spin on the ARM7's channel-ready bits at 0x027ffc00 + 0x388 and
# port/ntr models no IPC at all, so calling them never returns; func_02058ec8
# and func_02059594 reach func_02058764, which reads the Slot-2 magic at
# 0x08000000 and no ntr::kRegions entry covers that address. The header block
# of hal/boot_os.cpp lists every skipped step with its measurement.
#
# On the two targets that compile tests/walk_window.cpp, because that file is
# where the boot calls live. See port/slice_gate214.txt.
# ---- lane IPCSEND: the channel-8 firmware read, re-seated -------------------
# Four matched TUs run link100 lane BOOT2 backed out because the ARM9 could not
# send. It can now (IPCSend is in GATE2IPC_SYMS below), so func_020196cc goes
# back at its own point in hal/boot_os.cpp's port_boot_rom_game_init_tail. This
# list rides with SLICE214_SOURCES rather than with the PXI slice, because
# hal/boot_os.cpp is what calls it and that file is on the two walk_window
# targets only -- putting the four on smoke_player as well would add object
# files whose externs (data_0208ee3c, data_0209d4b8) that target does not host.
# See port/slice_ipcsend.txt.
port_read_lines("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/slice_ipcsend.txt" SLICE_IPCSEND_LINES)
set(SLICE_IPCSEND_SOURCES "")
foreach(line IN LISTS SLICE_IPCSEND_LINES)
    string(STRIP "${line}" line)
    if(line MATCHES "^#" OR line STREQUAL "")
        continue()
    endif()
    list(APPEND SLICE_IPCSEND_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../${line}")
endforeach()

port_read_lines("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/slice_gate214.txt" SLICE214_LINES)
# hal/globals_link100.cpp: the card driver's control block, hosted as the one
# ROM object dsd split into three names. It is on this list because that block
# is the storage the func_02042f68 refusal in hal/boot_os.cpp is about, and the
# refusal and the storage should not drift apart.
set(SLICE214_SOURCES hal/boot_os.cpp hal/boot_hw.cpp hal/boot_globals.cpp)
# hal/globals_link100.cpp rides beside ntr/backup.cpp on all three targets: the
# save gate's SaveData bodies reference the card span from smoke_player too.
foreach(line IN LISTS SLICE214_LINES)
    string(STRIP "${line}" line)
    if(line MATCHES "^#" OR line STREQUAL "")
        continue()
    endif()
    list(APPEND SLICE214_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../${line}")
endforeach()

# ---- run link100 rung R3F: THE THREE `G` PLACEHOLDERS THAT ARE REGISTERS ----
#
# Read blocker B4 in hal/boot_os.cpp's placeholder table first, and lane R3E's
# derivation (runs/link100/out/R3E/e1_blocker.txt) second. The short of it:
# `G` is the decomp's GENERIC placeholder for an absolute address a function
# pools, so several unrelated TUs spell completely different things with the
# same identifier. One of them means it: _ZN4Heap10SetDefaultEv's pool word at
# 0x0203c338 carries a RELOC (config/arm9/relocs.txt: from:0x0203c338
# kind:load to:0x020a0ea0), so THERE `G` really is Memory::defaultHeapPtr and
# the /alternatename in hal/lk4_solidheap_seat.cpp is right. Three others pool
# an I/O address with NO reloc, because an absolute register needs none:
#
#     func_02055454  pool 0x02055460  0x04000010  BG0HOFS/BG0VOFS, str (word)
#     func_02057128  pool 0x0205713c  0x04000204  EXMEMCNT, ldrh/orr 0x80/strh
#     func_02057140  pool 0x02057154  0x04000204  EXMEMCNT, ldrh/bic 0x80/strh
#
# and those three, resolving `G` through the alias, were reading and writing
# the DEFAULT HEAP POINTER. func_02019144's else arm calls func_02055454 with
# the BG0 scroll on every VBlank of every 3D level, which is 0, so under
# SM64DS_ROM_LOOP=1 the allocator's default heap went NULL once per frame and
# the next free faulted at Heap::Deallocate+0x3 (R3E, frame 31, levels
# 1/5/9/13). The other two are the same landmine on the card-lock path: they
# OR and AND bit 7 of that pointer through func_02057158/func_02057178.
#
# THE FIX IS IN THE DECOMP AND IT COSTS NOTHING. src/ now spells each register
# the way src/func_0205583c.c and src/func_02057320.cpp already spell theirs,
# and all three still byte-verify against the ROM -- BETTER than before, since
# the placeholder made the pool word a reloc slot the byte gate WILDCARDED and
# a literal address is compared for real:
#
#     tools/match.py func_02055454 0x02055454 0x10  4/4 words OK  2004/b56
#     tools/match.py func_02057128 0x02057128 0x18  6/6 words OK  2004/b56
#     tools/match.py func_02057140 0x02057140 0x18  6/6 words OK  2004/b56
#
# Spelling it is only half. port/ntr/io.cpp's rule is that a store reaches
# ntr::io_write only if its TU was rewritten by tools/hostgen.py; built plain
# it latches in the mapped window and triggers nothing. So the three go through
# hostgen exactly the way rung BSWAP took the ROM's frame swap
# (func_020190b8, the R3B_SWAP block above), with the same kill switch
# discipline: the arm is PRINTED ON EVERY CONFIGURE in both directions,
# because a CMake option() caches and a switch that announces only one arm
# silently keeps the wrong one.
#
# The three come off port/slice_gate214.txt, so the cut below is against
# SLICE214_SOURCES and has to sit after that list is built. SLICE214_SOURCES
# goes to walk_window and walk_window_hires only, and R3F_GREG_GEN is appended
# to exactly those two targets: the LINK SET does not change, only the route.
option(R3F_GREG_PLAIN
       "run link100 R3F: build the three register TUs PLAIN (pre-fix arm)"
       OFF)
set(R3F_GREG_SYMS
    func_02055454          # BG0HOFS/BG0VOFS, the VBlank display commit
    func_02057128          # EXMEMCNT |= 0x80
    func_02057140)         # EXMEMCNT &= ~0x80
list(LENGTH R3F_GREG_SYMS R3F_GREG_WANT)
# GREG2 (run link100 lane GREG2, 09-09): a fourth `G` I/O reader, found by R3F
# but left unowned -- src/func_0205f650.c pools 0x04000304 (POWCNT1) with NO
# reloc and reads bit 0, so through the SetDefault alias it was reading bit 0
# of Memory::defaultHeapPtr instead. Its caller src/func_02019a58.c is the
# wait loop `while (func_0205f66c(1) != 1)` that polls this bit for the LCDs
# to come back on. It ships off port/slice_gate220.txt, not slice_gate214.txt
# (Stage::Behavior's gate, not this one's), so it cannot be cut out of
# SLICE214_SOURCES above -- the cut against SLICE220_SOURCES is further down
# this file, right after that list is built, and kept in its OWN counter so
# this addition cannot silently perturb R3F's already-verified 3/3 SLICE214
# accounting. It rides the SAME R3F_GREG_PLAIN switch and the SAME hostgen
# discipline as the three above.
set(R3F_GREG2_SYMS func_0205f650)   # POWCNT1 & 1 -- the LCD-power wait read
set(R3F_GREG_ALL_SYMS ${R3F_GREG_SYMS} ${R3F_GREG2_SYMS})
if(R3F_GREG_PLAIN)
    message(STATUS "R3F: R3F_GREG_PLAIN=ON -- the four register TUs build "
                   "PLAIN. This is the PRE-FIX arm: the stores latch in the "
                   "mapped I/O window and no register is told, and the "
                   "POWCNT1 read (GREG2) sees whatever that window has "
                   "instead of the seeded value.")
else()
    message(STATUS "R3F: R3F_GREG_PLAIN=OFF -- the four register TUs route "
                   "through hostgen (shipped arm).")
endif()
set(R3F_GREG_GEN "")
if(NOT R3F_GREG_PLAIN)
    foreach(sym IN LISTS R3F_GREG_ALL_SYMS)
        set(sym_in "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/${sym}.c")
        if(NOT EXISTS "${sym_in}")
            set(sym_in "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/${sym}.cpp")
        endif()
        set(sym_out "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src/src/${sym}.cpp")
        add_custom_command(OUTPUT "${sym_out}"
            COMMAND python "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/hostgen.py"
                    --out "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src" ${sym}
            DEPENDS "${sym_in}"
                    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/hostgen.py"
            COMMENT "hostgen ${sym}")
        list(APPEND R3F_GREG_GEN "${sym_out}")
    endforeach()
endif()
# Cut the plain slice entries in the SAME block that adds the generated ones,
# for the BSWAP block's reason: the real net is the LINKER either way, and the
# count guard below is only a signpost for a reader looking at a failed link.
set(R3F_GREG_CUT 0)
set(SLICE214_SRC_R3F "")
foreach(src IN LISTS SLICE214_SOURCES)
    set(_cut OFF)
    if(NOT R3F_GREG_PLAIN)
        foreach(sym IN LISTS R3F_GREG_SYMS)
            if(src MATCHES "/${sym}\.(c|cpp)$")
                set(_cut ON)
            endif()
        endforeach()
    endif()
    if(_cut)
        math(EXPR R3F_GREG_CUT "${R3F_GREG_CUT}+1")
    else()
        list(APPEND SLICE214_SRC_R3F "${src}")
    endif()
endforeach()
set(SLICE214_SOURCES ${SLICE214_SRC_R3F})
if(R3F_GREG_PLAIN)
    set(R3F_GREG_CUT ${R3F_GREG_WANT})
endif()
if(NOT R3F_GREG_CUT EQUAL R3F_GREG_WANT)
    message(STATUS "R3F: expected to cut ${R3F_GREG_WANT} plain register-TU "
                   "entries and cut ${R3F_GREG_CUT}. If slice_gate214.txt "
                   "stopped listing one of them the hostgen copy is still "
                   "added and the link will say so; if a SECOND slice started "
                   "listing one, this cut missed it and the link will say that "
                   "too")
endif()

# ---- gate seat1 (run link100 wave 7, lane SEAT1) ---------------------------
#
# port/slice_seat1.txt carries the whole derivation, including the nine rows
# the REMAIN2 census assigned this lane that do NOT survive reading. Three do.
#
# ROW 1 is a dsd LABEL SHIFT and its fix is the alternatename guard's own R1/R2
# recipe, the one lane SMALLS used for the mother penguin's tenth TU: ov031,
# ov039 and ov044 share load base 0x021111a0, and the label picker gave ov031's
# own 0x02111214 a sibling's name in the one TU that calls it. The ROM's
# relocation is unambiguous (ov031/relocs.txt:14, from:0x0211132c
# kind:arm_call to:0x02111214 module:overlay(31)), so the CALLER is recompiled
# with a per-source -DLHS=RHS and ov031's body links under its own name.
# src/_ZN19daObjKb1Billboard_c20UpdateModelTransformEv.c keeps its own ov044 caller
# (_ZN19daObjKb1Billboard_c13InitResourcesEv, reloc from:0x021112c8
# to:0x02111214 module:overlay(44)) and stays in the link.
port_read_lines("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/slice_seat1.txt" SLICE_SEAT1_LINES)
set(SLICE_SEAT1_SOURCES "")
foreach(line IN LISTS SLICE_SEAT1_LINES)
    string(STRIP "${line}" line)
    if(line MATCHES "^#" OR line STREQUAL "")
        continue()
    endif()
    list(APPEND SLICE_SEAT1_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../${line}")
endforeach()
# RETIRED at the main->port sync (lane SYNC5). The label shift this -D worked
# around is gone on main: src/game/actors/d_a_obj_hs_billboard.cpp is the ov031
# TU that both DEFINES func_ov031_02111214 (its own @symbol, line 73) and CALLS
# it (line 49), so the caller no longer spells the callee with ov044's name and
# there is nothing left to rewrite. ov044's own body is
# _ZN19daObjKb1Billboard_c20UpdateModelTransformEv in
# src/game/actors/d_a_obj_kb1_billboard.cpp, a different TU with a different
# name, so the two no longer collide by spelling either. The slice_seat1 row
# that named the per-function file is quarantined for the same reason.
# set_source_files_properties(
#     "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/_ZN25SlideDecorationSilverStar13InitResourcesEv.cpp"
#     PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS "func_ov044_02111214=func_ov031_02111214")
#
# ROWS 2 AND 3 are R3F's recipe one bit over: src/func_020570c0.c and
# src/func_020570d8.c set and clear EXMEMCNT bit 11 (the NDS slot's ARM7/ARM9
# access right) and used to spell the address as the placeholder `G`, which
# resolves in this binary to the default-heap word. They now spell 0x04000204
# the way src/func_02057128.c and src/func_02057140.c do, one page down and one
# bit over, and both still byte-verify on 2004/b56 with the pool word compared
# for real. They ride the SAME R3F_GREG_PLAIN switch and the same hostgen
# discipline as R3F's three, in their OWN counter for the GREG2 reason: an

# They were never on a slice (port/slice_nitrofs.txt lists them under "NOT

# hal/nitrofs_face.cpp instead. Under R3F_GREG_PLAIN=ON the pair is not built at
# all and the link says so at the two call sites, which is the honest pre-fix

    func_020570d8)         # EXMEMCNT &= ~0x800, the card to the ARM9

            COMMAND python "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/hostgen.py"

# ---- gate 2ipc: the PXI layer (the ARM9<->ARM7 link) -----------------------
#
# port/docs/mmio-inventory.md counted eight IPC registers and zero modelled,
# and that zero is what kept the ROM's own inter-processor layer out of the
# link: src/func_0205bad8.c's IPCSYNC handshake never converged and four
# matched channel initialisers spun forever on an ARM7 readiness word nothing
# ever wrote. port/ntr/ipc.cpp is the register model (added to the three ntr
# libraries above, since ntr/io.cpp dispatches into it) and
# port/hal/boot2_ipc.cpp is the host ARM7 and the PXI bss. Neither is
# decompiled code. The nine matched TUs this makes linkable, the ROM edges
# that reach them and the four channels deliberately left out are all in
# port/slice_gate2ipc.txt.
#
# THREE OF THEM MUST BE HOSTGEN'D. func_0205bad8 reaches IPCSYNC through a
# pointer bound to a literal, so built plain its reads come off the mapped
# latch and the ARM7's nibble is always zero. IRQ::IPCRxFifoNotEmptyHandler
# reads IPCFIFORECV at 0x04100000, which is outside every region ntr/io.cpp
# maps -- built plain that is an access violation, not a stale read.
#
# IPCSend IS THE THIRD, and until run link100 lane IPCSEND it was the one that
# was missing. Its `*(volatile unsigned int *)0x4000188 = cmd.raw` is exactly
# hostgen's MMIO_DEREF shape, and built plain it LATCHED IN THE MAPPED WINDOW:
# this port had never made an ARM9->ARM7 send at all, which is why every
# [ipc:rom-boot] line in the tree read send=0, and why lane BOOT2 had to back
# func_020196cc out again (it hung at func_0205ff08 + 0 with data_020a8114 == 1,
# waiting for a reply to a request that was never delivered).
# ITS PLAIN LINE IS COMMENTED OUT OF port/slice_gate10.txt, and the two lists go
# to the same three targets, so the LINK SET does not change -- only the route.
# NOTHING ELSE ABOUT THE FUNCTION CHANGES. Its two IPCFIFOCNT reads used to come
# off the window ntr::ipc_publish keeps truthful and now come from
# ntr/ipc.cpp's fifocnt_value() directly, which is the same number by
# construction; its error arm's `|= 0xc000` stops being a store into a latch and
# becomes the acknowledge ipc_reg_write documents; and with SM64DS_IPC_MODEL=0
# ipc_reg_read/ipc_reg_write both decline, so io.cpp falls through to the same
# mapped window a plain build used and the negative control is untouched.
set(GATE2IPC_SYMS func_0205bad8 _ZN3IRQ24IPCRxFifoNotEmptyHandlerEv IPCSend)
set(GATE2IPC_GEN "")
foreach(sym IN LISTS GATE2IPC_SYMS)
    if(EXISTS "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/${sym}.c")
        set(sym_src "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/${sym}.c")
    else()
        set(sym_src "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/${sym}.cpp")
    endif()
    set(sym_out "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src/src/${sym}.cpp")
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT "${sym_out}"
        COMMAND python "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/hostgen.py"
                --out "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src" ${sym}
        DEPENDS "${sym_src}" "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/hostgen.py"
        COMMENT "hostgen ${sym}")
    list(APPEND GATE2IPC_GEN "${sym_out}")
endforeach()

    list(APPEND SLICE2IPC_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../${line}")
endforeach()

# ---- THE GAPLESS PER-ENTRY CORRECTION: the five G-adding OAM routers ---------
#
# Read THE ROUTER HOOK at the foot of port/hal/screen_gap.cpp before this. The
# gapless minigame mod zeroes the framework's screen-gap word, which takes G out
# of every submission these five bodies make to the top engine, and the fix has
# to put it back for THOSE submissions and for no others -- the score rows and
# the top screen's artwork are placed in screen space and were never displaced.
# Nothing in the finished OAM tells the two apart, so the routed set is recorded
# at the call, and this is the only place a call can be got at without editing
# src/.
#
# TWO RENAMES PER TU, and both are the R-series remedy this file already uses a
# dozen times over:
#
#   <router>=<router>__rom   the TU defines its body under a private name, and
#                            hal/screen_gap.cpp defines the real name as a
#                            wrapper that captures the world row and calls it.
#                            Every caller in the program links the wrapper.
#   OAM::Render=port_...     the TU declares its OAM::Render overload extern "C"
#                            by mangled name, so renaming that name redirects
#                            THAT TU's calls -- and only that TU's -- to the
#                            shim in hal/screen_gap.cpp. The overload's own
#                            definition, and every other caller of it in the
#                            program, is untouched.
#
# EACH FILE IS ON EXACTLY ONE SLICE and those slices ride smoke_player,
# walk_window and walk_window_hires, all three of which link hal/screen_gap.cpp,
# so the shims and wrappers are present wherever the renamed TUs are. Checked
# rather than assumed: the five appear once each across every port/slice_*.txt.
#
# WHICH OVERLOAD EACH TU CALLS, off the TU's own declaration:
#   func_ov004_020aff38   ..._Fix12IiEi        8 args   -> port_oam_render_routed_8
#   func_ov004_020afdd0   ..._Fix12IiES3_ii   10 args   -> port_oam_render_routed_10
#   func_ov004_020b023c   ...P9Matrix2x2       7 args   -> port_oam_render_routed_mtx
#   func_ov004_020b0380   ...P9Matrix2x2       7 args   -> port_oam_render_routed_mtx
#   RenderOamBothScreens  ...P9Matrix2x2       7 args   -> port_oam_render_routed_mtx
# func_ov004_020afdd0 also calls OAM::RenderSub for the bottom engine, which is
# a different symbol, is not renamed, and needs no correction: the bottom
# engine's y is the world row itself in every arm.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/func_ov004_020aff38.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "func_ov004_020aff38=func_ov004_020aff38__rom;_ZN3OAM6RenderEbP7OamAttriiii5Fix12IiEi=port_oam_render_routed_8")
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/func_ov004_020afdd0.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "func_ov004_020afdd0=func_ov004_020afdd0__rom;_ZN3OAM6RenderEbP7OamAttriiii5Fix12IiES3_ii=port_oam_render_routed_10")
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/func_ov004_020b023c.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "func_ov004_020b023c=func_ov004_020b023c__rom;_ZN3OAM6RenderEbP7OamAttriiiiP9Matrix2x2=port_oam_render_routed_mtx")
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/func_ov004_020b0380.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "func_ov004_020b0380=func_ov004_020b0380__rom;_ZN3OAM6RenderEbP7OamAttriiiiP9Matrix2x2=port_oam_render_routed_mtx")
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/RenderOamBothScreens.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "RenderOamBothScreens=RenderOamBothScreens__rom;_ZN3OAM6RenderEbP7OamAttriiiiP9Matrix2x2=port_oam_render_routed_mtx")

# src/game/actors/d_a_pg_mthr.cpp IS SLICED NOW, on port/slice_smalls.txt (gate
# smalls, below). It was not when this gate landed: its symbol was spoken for by
# gate 188's alias in unmatched/Jrb_Aliases.cpp
# (_func_ov018_02111bf0 -> _func_ov016_02111bf0), which three LINKED ov016
# UNAGI bodies depend on -- they spell their own module's 0x02111bf0 with the
# ov018 prefix, and ov016/ov018 share load base 0x021111a0. Defining the LHS
# DEFEATED that alias and rerouted Unagi into the mother penguin's collision
# pass; alternatename_guard.py failed this gate's first link on exactly that
# (LHS 0001:00188350 vs RHS 0001:00148d00), so the body was host copied under a
# port name in unmatched/MotherPenguin_ClsnPass.cpp and this gate's two callers
# were renamed onto it. Gate smalls applied the guard's own R1/R2 recipe
# instead -- the dead alternatename deleted, the three ov016 callers renamed
# per source onto func_ov016_02111bf0 -- so the ov018 name is free, both
# callers below reach the ROM's own body under its own name, and the host copy
# is retired. The rename that stood on func_ov018_02112234.c is gone with it.
# The literal at 0x02112230 is 0x02113bf0 and carries NO relocation row, so
# it is ov018's OWN bss -- the Animation SharedFilePtr __sinit_ov018_02112c80
# constructs with file id 0x406, which func_ov018_021122ec already reads as
# data_ov018_02113bf0[1]. The source's data_ov027 spelling is the
# #1308-#1310 cross-overlay family (ov018/ov022/ov027/ov036/ov056 share load
# base 0x021111a0 and are never co-resident) and the port DEFINES
# data_ov027_02113bf0 in ov027's own mount, so without this rename the link
# succeeds against the wrong storage. Renamed, not edited, the way
# _ZN13RollingLogLll16CleanupResourcesEv's func_021270dc is: the declaration
# is local to this TU and no header here declares either name, so the
# rewrite cannot collide.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/game/actors/d_a_pg_mthr.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS "data_ov027_02113bf0=data_ov018_02113bf0")
# RETIRED at the main -> port sync, lane FACES1. The rename that used to sit
# here read:
#
#     "func_ov018_021123d0=port_mpg_set_state_zero"
#
# and it existed because the legacy one-function TU DECLARED
# func_ov018_021123d0 with ONE parameter and called it with one, while the ROM
# body takes two (the ROM sets r1 = 0 at 0x02111ef8, a `mov r1,#0` the source
# spelled as the neighbouring `*(int*)(s+0x374) = 0`, which is why it still
# byte-matched on ARM). On x86 the missing second argument was a stack slot the
# caller never wrote: the callee read [ebp+0Ch], shifted it left by four and
# parked a wild pointer in self+0x370. port_mpg_set_state_zero, in
# unmatched/MotherPenguin_AfterClsnSeat.cpp, supplied the ROM's own 0.
#
# TWO THINGS CHANGED AT THE SYNC, and together they turn the rename from a fix
# into a defect:
#
#   1. main's consolidated src/game/actors/d_a_pg_mthr.cpp now DEFINES
#      func_ov018_021123d0 (line 297, `void func_ov018_021123d0(char *self,
#      int i)`), so a -D rename of that identifier renames the DEFINITION as
#      well as the calls, and the TU emitted a second port_mpg_set_state_zero
#      beside the seat file's. That was one of walk_window's 17 remaining
#      LNK2005 rows (runs/link100/out/ALIAS2/host_abi_conflicts.txt, the row
#      marked "THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT and is the cheapest of the seventeen").
#   2. every call site in that TU now spells BOTH arguments -- lines 206, 400,
#      445, 472, 504, 626, 691 and 711, each passing an explicit 0, 1 or 2 --
#      so there is nothing left for the shim to supply.
#
# So the rename is deleted rather than re-scoped: a -D cannot tell a definition
# from a call, and there is no call left that needs it. The seat file's
# port_mpg_set_state_zero stays defined and unreferenced, which /OPT:REF drops.
#
# AND THE ROW ABOVE COMES BACK. set_source_files_properties REPLACES a property
# rather than appending to it, and both blocks named the same file, so the
# data_ov027_02113bf0 -> data_ov018_02113bf0 rename immediately above was being
# overwritten by this one and had not been applied since the sync folded the
# two TUs together. Deleting this block restores it.

# R10, run rel0215 wave 3 (lane w3-b): THE R9 PREDICATE IS TOO NARROW BY ONE
# SHAPE, and this lane found the gap by CRASHING rather than by reading.
#
# R9 above defines the pointer-to-member width class as "a pointer-to-member of
# an INCOMPLETE class AND a NONZERO offset applied to it", and rules the pp[0]
# siblings "correct BY LUCK and deliberately NOT listed here". That reading has
# an unstated premise: that MSVC's default representation is the FOUR-BYTE one,
# so an index-0 read lands on the function word. It is four bytes only when the
# class is DEFINED SOMEWHERE IN THE SAME TU, which is true of every one of the
# twenty-one TUs R9 scanned -- they all spell
#     struct C; typedef void (C::*PMF)(); struct C { char pad[N]; PMF *pp; };
# and MSVC picks the representation from C's real (single-inheritance) layout.
#
# src/_ZN8Snowball8BehaviorEv.cpp NEVER DEFINES ITS CLASS. It spells
#     struct Klass; typedef void (Klass::*PMF)();
#     struct M { char pad[8]; PMF pmf; };
#     M *m = *(M **)&unk_378;  if (m->pmf != 0) (this->*(m->pmf))();
# and `Klass` is never completed, so MSVC falls back to the MOST GENERAL
# representation -- SIXTEEN bytes, {fn, delta, vbptr offset, vbindex}. The
# index is still zero and it still breaks, because the width decides where the
# FIELDS are, not just the stride. MEASURED, in the obj and then in a crash:
#
#   without the option, the FULL measured sequence (the out-of-bounds reads
#   are CONDITIONAL; the fault fires because the garbage "vbindex" word past
#   the cell is nonzero, which routes the guarded virtual path):
#                         mov edx,[esi+378h]     ; the cell
#                         mov edi,[edx+8]        ; fn        -- correct
#                         push ebx
#                         mov ebx,[edx+14h]      ; "vbindex" -- past the cell
#                         test ebx,ebx           ; guard: zero would take the
#                         jne .virt              ;   non-virtual path and live
#                         mov eax,[edx+0Ch]      ; (not taken here)
#                         jmp .join
#                  .virt: mov ecx,[edx+10h]      ; "vbptr"   -- past the cell
#                         mov eax,[ecx+esi]
#                         mov eax,[eax+ebx]      <- FAULT, +0x37
#                         add eax,ecx
#                         add eax,[edx+0Ch]
#   The ROM cell is SIXTEEN bytes TOTAL (enter {fn,delta} then tick {fn,delta}),
#   so [edx+10h] and [edx+14h] are past the end of the record entirely.
#   FAULT c0000005 at ?Behavior@Snowball@@QAEHXZ+0x37 accessing 78531c75,
#   walker node id 0xe0, frame 1 of
#   SM64DS_LEVEL=19 SM64DS_SPAWN_ACTOR=224 SM64DS_FAULTS_FATAL=1.
#
#   with /vmg /vmm        sizeof(PMF) is 8, so `m->pmf` is {[m+8], [m+0Ch]} --
#                         exactly the ROM's tick record -- and the call adds
#                         delta (zero on both of Snowball's records) to `this`
#                         and jumps to fn. The ROM's own dispatch.
#
# THE OTHER THREE PMF SITES IN THIS SEAT WERE DISASSEMBLED TOO rather than
# assumed, and all three are right as they stand:
#   func_ov081_021261d4  Snowball's installer -- 4-byte PMF (its `struct C` IS
#                        defined in the TU), reads [pp] = the enter fn, and
#                        tail-JUMPS, so the host body reads its receiver off
#                        the reused cdecl frame. R9's index-0 case, genuinely.
#   _ZN8daGmch_c14CallStateEnterEv  Moneybag's enter dispatcher -- same shape, same
#                        4-byte read of [pp], same tail jump.
#   _ZN8daGmch_c15CallStateUpdateEv  Moneybag's tick dispatcher -- ALREADY on R9's list
#                        above; with the option it reads [pp+0Ch] as delta and
#                        [pp+8] as fn, which is the tick record. Confirmed in
#                        the obj, not taken on trust.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/_ZN8Snowball8BehaviorEv.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "/vmg;/vmm")

# R11, run rel0215 wave 3 (lane w3-d, ov070 FlyGuy): THE PMF CALLING
# CONVENTION IS A PROPERTY OF THE SITE, NOT THE CLASS. Before seating raw
# cdecl bodies into a pointer-to-member table, disassemble EVERY live
# dispatch site from the build's own objects. A site MSVC compiles as a
# one-call forwarder ends `pop ebp / jmp eax` and reuses the caller's cdecl
# frame, so the receiver is still at [esp+4] and a raw body is correct. A
# site that does work after the dispatch cannot be a forwarder: it emits
# `call eax` with the receiver in ECX and NOTHING PUSHED, and needs a
# __fastcall thunk (push ecx / call / add esp,4 / ret). The two sets can be
# disjoint halves of the SAME class's cells -- FlyGuy's enter halves are
# tail-jumped and its tick halves are not.
#
# THIS FAILURE IS SILENT. With the wrong convention live,
# func_ov070_0211fa80 wrote *(int*)(c+0x3dc)=0 through a stray pointer
# every FlyGuy frame while the byte gate, the linkage count, all five ABI
# checkers, the guards, the census and rc stayed green. The only instrument
# that caught it was a before/after state trace (level 19 player y: 720.1
# flat with the raw seat vs 800-820 oscillating with the thunks). Enumerate
# sites by disassembly, never by grepping for a source shape -- FlyGuy's
# Behavior reads a Holder{char pad[8]; PMF fn;} at +8, which R9's
# `c->pp + 1` grep could not see.
#
# THE MAP GIVES A FAST FIRST READ (run rel0215, lanes prop16/prop17): grep
# walk_window.map for the DISPATCHER symbol and read the .obj column. A
# dispatcher from a src/*.cpp.obj is MSVC's own lowering of a real
# member-pointer call: receiver in ECX, nothing pushed -- seat a
# __fastcall(self, dummy) thunk. A dispatcher from a port/unmatched/*.obj
# host copy has usually rewritten the call as void(*)(void*): plain cdecl
# indirect call, receiver on the stack -- seat the bare cdecl body, and a
# thunk would MIS-RECEIVE (ov074's state 0 puts state_index*16 = 0 in ECX,
# so the thunked call hands the body a null this). The .obj column decides
# the DEFAULT; the per-site disassembly above remains the confirmation,
# because one class's halves can split (FlyGuy) and a forwarder can hide in
# a src obj. Fastcall iff no push of the receiver before the call.

# R12, run rel0215 (lane tagfix): THE PREDICATE MISSES A RUNTIME INDEX, AND
# THE WIDTH IT LANDS ON IS THE SIXTEEN-BYTE ONE, MEASURED.
#
# R9 finds its twenty-one TUs by scanning src/ for "a pointer-to-member of an
# INCOMPLETE class AND a NONZERO offset applied to it", and every one of those
# offsets is a LITERAL -- `pp + 1`, `pp[2]`, a `+ 8` in a guard. So the sweep
# is blind to a site whose index is a RUNTIME VALUE, which is exactly the shape
# of src/_ZN10BrickBlock8BehaviorEv.cpp:
#
#     struct C; typedef void (C::*PMF)();
#     extern "C" PMF data_ov002_0210dd30[];
#     ...
#     int idx = unk_0d7;                     <- 0..3, written by InitResources
#     (((C*)((char*)this))->*data_ov002_0210dd30[idx])();
#
# Nothing in that source spells an offset at all. The index comes from the
# actor's own id at InitResources time (0x141 -> 0, 0x142 -> 1, 0x143 -> 2,
# 0x144 -> 3), so three of the four live ids stride, and a grep cannot see it.
#
# MEASURED IN THIS LANE'S OWN BASE OBJECT, not derived. R9 says MSVC's default
# is FOUR bytes and R10 says it is SIXTEEN when the class is never completed.
# This TU does complete `struct C` -- but only AFTER the array of pointers to
# members of it has been declared -- and MSVC takes the general form:
#
#   base, no option        movzx eax,byte ptr [edi+0D7h]   ; idx
#                          shl   eax,4                     ; idx * SIXTEEN
#                          mov   ecx,_data_ov002_0210dd30[eax+4]
#                          mov   eax,_data_ov002_0210dd30[eax]
#                          add   ecx,edi
#                          call  eax
#
# `shl eax,4` is the whole defect. data_ov002_0210dd30 is THIRTY-TWO bytes of
# bss (0x0210dd30..0x0210dd50, four 8-byte records) and the four indices read:
#
#     idx 0  ->  +0   record 0, correct by luck
#     idx 1  ->  +16  record 2's function word -- the WRONG handler
#     idx 2  ->  +32  PAST THE ARRAY, into whatever the linker put next
#     idx 3  ->  +48  further past
#
# and idx 0 and 1 then CALL what they read, which until this lane's seat is a
# raw DS text address (0x020b429c / 0x020b41f8), mapped-but-NX on the host.
# There is no benign index: every one of the four ids is a fault.
#
# With /vmg /vmm sizeof(PMF) is 8. No shift is emitted at all -- the multiply
# folds into the scaled index, so the `shl` disappears and the two reads become
#                          mov ecx,_data_ov002_0210dd30[eax*8+4]
#                          mov eax,_data_ov002_0210dd30[eax*8]
# which is the record's own {fn, delta} -- the ROM's dispatch exactly. Both
# halves of the fix are needed and neither is sufficient alone: the width puts
# the read on the right record, and hal/actor_classes_bob_world.cpp's
# port_itemtag_states_seat() puts a HOST address in that record. The seat
# verifies the four ROM words before rewriting and aborts on anything else.
#
# THE CALL IS NOT A FORWARDER, so R11 applies and the four bodies cannot be
# seated raw. `call eax` with the receiver in ECX and NOTHING PUSHED -- the
# TU does real work after the dispatch (MarkForDestruction, then `return 1`),
# which is R11's own test for a frame that cannot be tail-jumped. The four
# matched bodies are flat cdecl C names taking `char *`, so the seat points
# the table at four __fastcall thunks rather than at the bodies themselves.
# Read off this lane's build, before and after, in the lane's evidence.
#
# PER-SOURCE, NEVER GLOBAL, R9's rule unchanged. This TU includes only
# BrickBlock.h (which declares no `::*`) and its own four-line struct, so
# nothing crosses a header boundary and no type in it changes size.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/_ZN10BrickBlock8BehaviorEv.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "/vmg;/vmm")

# run rel0215 wave 3, lane w3-b: the ONE fall-off-the-end body in this seat.

                --out "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src" ${sym}
        DEPENDS "${sym_src}" "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/hostgen.py"
        COMMENT "hostgen ${sym}")

endforeach()

            "unmatched/ModelAnim_Renders.cpp). Both would define the same "
            "symbol (LNK2005). Remove the slice line.")
    endif()
endforeach()

                   "the hostgen copy is still added and the link will say so; "
                   "if a SECOND slice started listing it, this cut missed it "
                   "and the link will say that too")

# Cloud::InitResources carries TWO sibling-overlay spellings of addresses
# that are ov039's own in this class's module: it calls
# _ZN19daObjKb1Billboard_c20UpdateModelTransformEv and bumps data_ov041_021118e0, while the ROM relocs
# at 0x02111354 and 0x02111378 both read module:overlay(39). Routed per
# source, which a definition cannot defeat the way an /alternatename can.
# func_ov039_02111214 is the matched TU on slice_gate217;
# data_ov039_021118e0 is the four-byte counter the fill defines.
# lane CDEFS 2026-09-16: a dead COMPILE_DEFINITIONS row stood here.
# A LATER set_source_files_properties() names d_a_obj_kumo.cpp for the same
# property, and that call REPLACES this one, so nothing on this row ever
# reached the compiler. Each definition it carried, against the synced TU:
#   _ZN19daObjKb1Billboard_c20UpdateModelTransformEv=func_ov039_02111214  --  dead, the TU does not spell _ZN19daObjKb1Billboard_c20UpdateModelTransformEv
#   data_ov041_021118e0=data_ov039_021118e0  --  dead, the TU does not spell data_ov041_021118e0
# Deleted rather than merged. The surviving row is unchanged.
# Cloud::Behavior is a flat .c TU that spells decl_common.h's two generic
# placeholder names, FindWithActorID and SetPolygonID. Both are real arm9
# functions the ROM relocs name outright -- 0x02010ef0
# _ZN8dActor_c15FindWithActorIDEjPS_ and 0x02016abc _ZN5Model12SetPolygonIDEi,
# read out of config/arm9/overlays/ov039/relocs.txt inside the Behavior
# span -- and both already have a C-linkage definition in this link
# (hal/actor_faces_bob.cpp aliases the static onto its ROM name;
# hal/actor_classes_ov063.cpp defines the SetPolygonID face for exactly
# this reason). Bound PER SOURCE rather than by a global /alternatename on
# a bare placeholder name, so no other TU that spells either word is
# steered by this lane.

# lane cast-ov030, TRAP: THREE ov030 TUs SPELL A VTABLE WITH THE WRONG NAME AND
# TWO SPELL IT WITH A PLACEHOLDER. Each rename is read off that TU's OWN literal
# pool in config/arm9/overlays/ov030/relocs.txt, the ov043 trap-4 discipline
# (line 8300 above), never guessed from the placeholder's usual meaning.
#
#   src/d_a_obj_hm_maruta.c   stores TWO tables, in this ROM order:
#       from:0x02111680 -> 0x02128338  _ZTV13daObjMaruta_c, an INTERMEDIATE base
#                                      table that lives in ov080 (level 22 loads
#                                      ov080, not ov078, so that is the live
#                                      spelling of `module:overlays(79,80)`);
#                                      already mounted by port/ov080_syms.txt
#       from:0x02111684 -> 0x02115a48  the class's OWN table, the host array
#     and src spells them `_ZTV15daObjHmMaruta_c` then `VT1` -- the FIRST name is
#     on the WRONG store. VT1 is renamed to _ZTV13RollingLogTtm rather than straight
#     to _ZTV15daObjHmMaruta_c because a macro whose body is another macro is
#     rescanned and both stores would collapse onto the same array.
#     _ZTV13RollingLogTtm is config's own (mis-attributed) name for 0x02115a48 and
#     hal/actor_classes_ov030.cpp aliases it onto the one host array with
#     /alternatename, so this is ONE storage under two names -- the
#     _ZTV10dBgActor_c / _ZTV10dBgActor_c shape at hal/actor_classes.cpp:591.
#
#   src/_ZN13RollingLogTtmD1Ev.cpp and src/_ZN13RollingLogTtmD0Ev.cpp (BOTH are really
#   RollingLogTtm's destructors) store THREE tables, ROM order:
#       0x02115a48  the class's own      -- spelled _ZTV15daObjHmMaruta_c, RIGHT
#       0x02128338  ov080's intermediate -- spelled _ZTV10dBgActor_c,      WRONG
#       0x0210ae38  Platform's base      -- spelled VT2, a placeholder
#     0x0210ae38 is config's _ZTV10dBgActor_c, which hal/actor_classes.cpp already
#     defines and fills (it fills _ZTV10dBgActor_c and _ZTV10dBgActor_c with the
#     same contents for exactly this reason), so VT2 goes straight to it.
#     Neither replacement is itself a macro here, so no rescan collision.
#     D0 additionally spells the heap `G0`; its pool word is 0x0211160c ->
#     0x020a0eac, the same global _ZN7daMky_cD0Ev.c names outright.
#
#   src/_ZN13daObjHmBskt_cD0Ev.cpp (UkikiCage's D0) spells all three by placeholder;
#     its pool is 0x02111240 -> 0x02115974, 0x02111244 -> 0x0210ae38 and
#     0x02111248 -> 0x020a0eac, so VT0/VT1/G0 map to the class's own table,
#     Platform's base and the heap. Its sibling src/_ZN13daObjHmBskt_cD1Ev.cpp (the
#     D1) spells the SAME pair BY NAME and correctly, and needs no rename.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/d_a_obj_hm_maruta.c"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "_ZTV15daObjHmMaruta_c=_ZTV13daObjMaruta_c;VT1=_ZTV13RollingLogTtm")
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/_ZN13RollingLogTtmD1Ev.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "_ZTV10dBgActor_c=_ZTV13daObjMaruta_c;VT2=_ZTV10dBgActor_c")
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/_ZN13RollingLogTtmD0Ev.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "_ZTV10dBgActor_c=_ZTV13daObjMaruta_c;VT2=_ZTV10dBgActor_c;G0=data_020a0eac")
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/_ZN13daObjHmBskt_cD0Ev.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "VT0=_ZTV13daObjHmBskt_c;VT1=_ZTV10dBgActor_c;G0=data_020a0eac")
# lane cast-ov030, the SECOND rename shape: src/actors/daMky_c.cpp calls
# three arm9 helpers by their func_ADDRESS PLACEHOLDER while config names all
# three and the port already links them under those real names. Measured off
# the first link's own unresolved list, then read back out of
# config/arm9/symbols.txt rather than guessed from the call site:
#   0x0203cfdc  line 1644  Vec3_Dist
#   0x0200f97c  line  234  _ZN8dActor_c13SpawnSoundObjEj
#   0x02015024  line  500  _ZN5dCc_c5ClearEv
# All three are already in walk_window.map on the BASE tree as _Vec3_Dist,
# __ZN8dActor_c13SpawnSoundObjEj and __ZN5dCc_c5ClearEv, so this is a
# spelling bridge onto bodies that already link and adds no TU to the count.
# BOTH PATHS, run link100 lane HOSTGEN4. This TU is on PORT_HOSTGEN_TU now,
# so the compile the build runs is the generated copy. These three renames
# are what bind the placeholder spellings to bodies that already link; on
# the raw path alone they would go missing and the three names would come
# straight back onto the unresolved wall. The src/ row is kept so the
# property is still right if the substitution is ever retired.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/actors/daMky_c.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src/src/actors/daMky_c.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "func_0203cfdc=Vec3_Dist;func_0200f97c=_ZN8dActor_c13SpawnSoundObjEj;func_02015024=_ZN5dCc_c5ClearEv")
# lane cast-ov030, THE G0/G1 TRAP, LIVE, and this row is the whole reason
# port/tools/alias_audit.py exists (its own docstring opens on this shape).
# src/_ZN13daObjHmBskt_c16CleanupResourcesEv.cpp is UkikiCage's CleanupResources and it Releases TWO
# SharedFilePtrs, spelled G0 and G1. hal/cxx_aliases.cpp binds those names ONCE
# for the whole link -- _G0 to _data_020a0eac (the GAME HEAP POINTER, line 1272)
# and _G1 to _data_ov002_0210e05c (an ov002 SharedFilePtr, line 1721) -- so
# without this row that function would have called SharedFilePtr::Release on the
# game heap pointer and on another overlay's object every time the cage tore
# down. It fails at NO link, shows in NO map, and no byte gate can see it.
# WHAT THE TU ACTUALLY MEANS, decoded from its own literal pool in the shipped
# image rather than from the placeholder's usual meaning:
#   0x0211132c  ldr r0,[pc,#0x14] -> 0x02111348 = 0x02115c88  = G0
#   0x02111334  ldr r0,[pc,#0x10] -> 0x0211134c = 0x02115c80  = G1
# Both are ov030's own .bss SharedFilePtrs and both are mounted by
# port/ov030_syms.txt. A comment-stripped sweep of all 67 slice TUs for
# G0/G1/G2/VT/VT0/VT1/VT2/HEAP/R0/R1/R2 finds placeholders in exactly five
# files, and all five are bound per source by the rows above and this one.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/_ZN13daObjHmBskt_c16CleanupResourcesEv.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "G0=data_ov030_02115c88;G1=data_ov030_02115c80")

# THE TWO SHARED-WINDOW ALIAS RACES (T6). ov017/ov023/ov035/ov045/ov055/ov056
# all link at 0x021111a0 and the decomp was written against whichever dsd
# export won the naming race, so two ov035 TUs spell ov035's own bytes with a
# sibling overlay's name. data_ov045_02112cb0 IS DEFINED in this link
# (port/ov045_syms.txt:123 mounts it), so an /alternatename with it on the left
# would be defeated silently -- the R3 ov071/ov073 failure -- and left alone
# the ov035 sinit would construct a SharedFilePtr over LEVEL 37's mounted data.
# A -D is the remedy T6 prescribes. The second is routed the same way so the

set_source_files_properties(

# ---- lane cast-ov066: THE SIX ALIASES THIS MOUNT DEFEATS --------------------
# THE TREE PREDICTED THIS LANE IN WRITING. port/build-port.cmd:92 and
# port/tools/alternatename_guard.py:20 both say "EyerokD0 and the data_ov075
# aliases flip the same way if their overlays land". SIX live /alternatename
# directives carried an ov066 name as their LHS, and defining that name defeats
# the alias SILENTLY -- no link error, a wrong object at run time, the
# Coffin/Spindrift shape. All six are removed from their hal files and replaced
# by per-source -D renames on the FOREIGN CALLER, which is the remedy
# hal/actor_classes_koopa_chuckya.cpp's own note already prescribes for exactly
# this case (the w5b_review.md R2 func_ov065_02117994 precedent).
#
# Every one was checked BOTH ways before the conversion: the caller TU is on a
# live slice, and the -D target is defined in the link. A -D onto an undefined
# name would have turned a silent bug into a link error, which is better, but
# neither is what this lane is for.
#
# (1) src/actors/daYurei_Mucho_c.cpp (slice_w5b) -- a Snufit state body. It calls
#     0x02115f84 and the reloc `from:0x02116314 kind:arm_call to:0x02115f84
#     module:overlay(65)` puts that body in ov065's OWN image as
#     func_ov065_02115f84, size 0x6c. Eyerok's D0 at the same address is size
#     0xb8 -- a DIFFERENT body, and the sizes alone settle it. Undefeated this
#     calls a destructor on a live Snufit.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/actors/daYurei_Mucho_c.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "_ZN6EyerokD0Ev=func_ov065_02115f84")
# (2) src/func_ov062_02117acc.c (slice_gate182) -- a Chuckya/Koopa body whose

    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "func_ov066_02118cdc=func_ov062_02118cdc;func_ov066_02118a50=func_ov062_02118a50")
# (3) src/func_ov060_02111c68.c (slice_w5e) and (4) src/func_ov060_02112350.c

# ---- lane cast-ov036: SIX PER-SOURCE PLACEHOLDER AND CROSS-NAME BINDINGS ----
# Every one is settled from the TU's OWN literal pool in
# config/arm9/overlays/ov036/relocs.txt, disassembled out of
# extracted/overlays/overlay_0036.bin, never by name. VT0/VT1/VT2 are the
# dangerous half: all three are DEFINED in this link (actor_vtables.cpp:407,
# `int VT0[20]` and its siblings), so an unrenamed store lands silently on a
# twenty-word shared dummy instead of failing at link -- the CMakeLists:2600
# class. G1 is the safe half (no cdecl row, so it would be a hard link error),
# and bare G0 in a .c resolves through `/alternatename:_G0=_data_020a0eac`,
# which is RIGHT for the three deleting destructors whose pools hold the game
# heap and WRONG for the one Cleanup whose pool holds its own two files.
#
# (1) src/game/actors/d_a_obj_rc_buranko.cpp -- SWINGING_PLATFORM's D0. Pool, in store order:
#     0x02111230 -> 0x02113a98 (its own table, host storage) and
#     0x02111234 -> 0x0210ae38 (_ZTV10dBgActor_c, the dBgActor_c base, already
#     host-filled by hal_fill_platform_vtable). Its G0 is NOT renamed: the third
#     pool word 0x02111238 -> 0x020a0eac module:main is the game heap
#     Memory::Deallocate takes, which is exactly what the cdecl row binds.
# lane CDEFS 2026-09-16: a dead COMPILE_DEFINITIONS row stood here.
# A LATER set_source_files_properties() names d_a_obj_rc_buranko.cpp for the same
# property, and that call REPLACES this one, so nothing on this row ever
# reached the compiler. Each definition it carried, against the synced TU:
#   VT0=_ZTV16daObjRcBuranko_c  --  dead, the TU does not spell VT0
#   VT1=_ZTV10dBgActor_c  --  dead, the TU does not spell VT1
# Deleted rather than merged. The surviving row is unchanged.
# (2) src/game/actors/d_a_obj_rc_buranko.cpp -- SWINGING_PLATFORM's CleanupResources.
#     Releases two SharedFilePtrs as G0/G1, and its own pool names them:
#     0x021112c0 -> 0x02114028 then 0x021112c4 -> 0x02114020, both
#     module:overlay(36), both in this lane's own mount. Unrenamed, G0 would
#     Release the game heap and G1 would not link. Renamed straight to the mount
#     names rather than to private ones: include/decl_common.h declares neither
#     data_ov036_02114020 nor data_ov036_02114028, so there is nothing to
#     conflict with (the ov043 TRAP-3 reading; the ov100 C2040 needed private
#     names only because the target was already declared as a scalar).
# lane CDEFS 2026-09-16: a dead COMPILE_DEFINITIONS row stood here.
# A LATER set_source_files_properties() names d_a_obj_rc_buranko.cpp for the same
# property, and that call REPLACES this one, so nothing on this row ever
# reached the compiler. Each definition it carried, against the synced TU:
#   G0=data_ov036_02114028  --  dead, the TU does not spell G0
#   G1=data_ov036_02114020  --  dead, the TU does not spell G1
# Deleted rather than merged. The surviving row is unchanged.
# (3) src/game/actors/d_a_obj_rc_kaitendai.cpp -- NO COMPILE_DEFINITIONS AT ALL,
#     AND THAT IS THE FIX (wave 10, lane UNHOSTED). Before the main-to-port sync
#     this class was three one-function files, each with a row of its own:
#       src/func_ov036_02111444.c (D1)
#         _ZTV19daObjRc_Kaitendai_c=data_ov036_02113b74;_ZTV10dBgActor_c=data_ov002_021091d4;VT2=_ZTV8Platform
#       src/func_ov036_02111494.c (D0)
#         VT0=data_ov036_02113b74;VT1=data_ov002_021091d4;VT2=_ZTV8Platform
#       src/RotatingPlatformRr_Spawn.c (the factory)
#         _ZTV19daObjRc_Kaitendai_c=data_ov002_021091d4;VT1=data_ov036_02113b74
#     The factory row existed because the RECOVERED source spelled the BASE store
#     with the DERIVED class's name. The synced TU does not. Its
#     daObjRc_Kaitendai_c_classInit writes
#       p[0] = (int)_ZTV16daObjKaitendai_c;     the ov002 intermediate, 0x021091d4
#       p[0] = (int)_ZTV19daObjRc_Kaitendai_c;  its own table,          0x02113b74
#     which is the cartridge's own order and the cartridge's own two values:
#       0211155c ldr r1,[pc,#0x14] -> 0x02111578 -> 0x021091d4 daObjKaitendai_c
#       02111560 ldr r0,[pc,#0x14] -> 0x0211157c -> 0x02113b74 its own table
#       02111564 str r1,[r4]   02111568 str r0,[r4]
#     and the TU spells no VT0/VT1/VT2/G0 placeholder anywhere. It does not write
#     the destructors either: the inline ~daObjRc_Kaitendai_c() in the header is
#     the whole source of both variants, so _ZTV10dBgActor_c never appears in it.
#     The three rows were carried across the sync BY NAME instead of by address,
#     and only the LAST set_source_files_properties for a file takes effect, so

#     daSnmBth_c_classInit's own pool holds the same two words and spells them
