# NINE PER-SOURCE BINDINGS, and every one is settled from the TU's OWN literal
# pool in config/arm9/overlays/ov047/relocs.txt, disassembled out of
# extracted/overlays/overlay_0047.bin, never by name.
#
# THE RECOVERED SOURCE USES THE RTTI-DERIVED VTABLE NAMES AND GETS THE CLASS
# RIGHT EVERY TIME -- but in the three factories it gets the ORDER backwards.
# The ROM stores the ov002 INTERMEDIATE BASE first and the class's OWN table
# second, which is the correct constructor order:
#   02111298 ldr r1,[pc,#0x14] -> 0x021112b4 -> 0x02109320   the base
#   0211129c ldr r0,[pc,#0x14] -> 0x021112b8 -> 0x021122a0   its own table
#   021112a0 str r1,[r4]   021112a4 str r0,[r4]
# while src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km3_kurumajiku.cpp writes `p[0] = _ZTV21daObjKm3_Kurumajiku_c;`
# FIRST and `p[0] = VT1;` second. So in the three factories the RTTI name means
# the BASE and VT1 means the own table; in the six destructors the same RTTI
# name means the OWN table. Both readings are bound per source. Left alone the
# factories would install the abstract intermediate LAST, and every one of these
# actors would dispatch InitResources through a table whose slot 0 is ZERO in
# the ROM -- a null call on the first frame, invisible to both the byte gate and
# the linkage count.
#
# _ZTV10dBgActor_c IS THE OTHER TRAP, the ov036 (3) one: three destructors spell
# their ov002 INTERMEDIATE base that way, and the port defines _ZTV10dBgActor_c
# as the PLATFORM base (0x0210ae38). Unrenamed those bodies would store the
# Platform table where the ROM stores the intermediate.
# id 153's five TUs need no rename at all: they spell _ZTV17daObjKm3_Dorifu_c,
# _ZTV13daObjDorifu_c and _ZTV10dBgActor_c, which are the three addresses the ROM
# writes, in the ROM's own order.
#
# SUPERSEDED FOR THE THREE FACTORIES (wave 10, lane UNHOSTED). Everything above
# describes the PRE-SYNC recovered sources. The synced TUs spell all three
# factories in the cartridge's own order, base first and own table second, under
# their real names and with no VT1 anywhere, so the three factory rows are gone;
# each class says so in its own block below.
# src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km3_kurumajiku.cpp -- NO COMPILE_DEFINITIONS AT ALL, same stale-by-name
# family as d_a_obj_km3_kaitendai.cpp above (wave 10, lane UNHOSTED). Three rows
# came across the sync, the TU merge collapsed them onto one path, and only the
# last one takes effect: _ZTV21daObjKm3_Kurumajiku_c=_ZTV17daObjKurumajiku_c. The synced
# TU spells its own factory correctly --
#   *(int *)actor = (int)_ZTV17daObjKurumajiku_c;
#   *(int *)actor = (int)&_ZTV21daObjKm3_Kurumajiku_c[2];
# and the cartridge's relocation run for the factory at 0x02111280 says the same pair
# in the same order:
#   from:0x021112b4 kind:load to:0x02109320   _ZTV17daObjKurumajiku_c (the ov002 intermediate)
#   from:0x021112b8 kind:load to:0x021122a0   its own table
# so the rename turned both stores into the abstract intermediate. id 152 RICKSHAW_BS, ov047, levels 39 and 40.
# src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km3_kaitendai.cpp -- NO COMPILE_DEFINITIONS AT ALL, AND
# THAT IS THE FIX (wave 10, lane UNHOSTED). This is the ov036 (3) case one
# overlay over: the same three rows the pre-sync one-function files carried (D1,
# D0, and the factory's mis-bound name) were brought across the sync BY NAME and
# collapsed onto one path when the TU merged. Only the LAST
# set_source_files_properties for a file takes effect, so the row that actually
# ran was the factory one, _ZTV20daObjKm3_Kaitendai_c=_ZTV16daObjKaitendai_c.
# The synced TU needs none of them. Its daObjKm3_Kaitendai_c_classInit writes
#   *(int *)actor = (int)_ZTV16daObjKaitendai_c;        the ov002 intermediate
#   *(int *)actor = (int)&_ZTV20daObjKm3_Kaitendai_c[2]; its own table
# (hostgen rewrites the +8 address point to the host array's own start, which is
# where the port's tables put slot 0), and the cartridge's own relocation run for
# the factory at 0x021113bc says exactly that pair, in that order:
#   from:0x021113f0 kind:load to:0x021091d4 module:overlay(2)    daObjKaitendai_c
#   from:0x021113f4 kind:load to:0x0211237c module:overlay(47)   its own table
# With the stale row in place both stores wrote the abstract intermediate, so
# every ROTATING_PLATFORM_BS on level 39 dispatched slot 0 into ov36_base_trap0
# ("UNHOSTED: vtable slot 0 (abstract base InitResources)"). The TU spells no
# VT0/VT1/VT2/G0 placeholder and does not name _ZTV10dBgActor_c anywhere.
# src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km3_kuruma.cpp -- NO COMPILE_DEFINITIONS AT ALL, same stale-by-name
# family as d_a_obj_km3_kaitendai.cpp above (wave 10, lane UNHOSTED). Three rows
# came across the sync, the TU merge collapsed them onto one path, and only the
# last one takes effect: _ZTV17daObjKm3_Kuruma_c=_ZTV13daObjKuruma_c. The synced
# TU spells its own factory correctly --
#   *(int *)actor = (int)_ZTV13daObjKuruma_c;
#   *(int *)actor = (int)&_ZTV17daObjKm3_Kuruma_c[2];
# and the cartridge's relocation run for the factory at 0x021114d0 says the same pair
# in the same order:
#   from:0x02111508 kind:load to:0x02109278   _ZTV13daObjKuruma_c (the ov002 intermediate)
#   from:0x0211150c kind:load to:0x0211244c   its own table
# so the rename turned both stores into the abstract intermediate. id 151 RICKSHAW_PLATFORM_BS, ov047, levels 39 and 40.
# FOUR WRONG-NAMES AT THE SHARED WINDOW (T6), all in one sinit. STAIRS_BS's file
# constructor spells FOUR of its own .bss symbols with an OV052 tag, and ov052
# IS MOUNTED (PORT_ACTOR_OVERLAYS), so all four resolve: the sinit would
# construct three SharedFilePtrs and register one destructor chain node in
# MARIO'S KEY COURSE's storage instead of its own. The ROM's own pool words at
# 0x02111958, 0x02111970, 0x0211197c and 0x0211196c all resolve to
# module:overlay(47). decl_common.h declares none of the eight names, so the
# renames are direct.
set_source_files_properties(

    "data_ov052_02112680=data_ov047_02112680;data_ov052_02112688=data_ov047_02112688;data_ov052_02112690=data_ov047_02112690;data_ov052_021126a8=data_ov047_021126a8")
list(APPEND SWEEP2_SOURCES hal/actor_classes_ov047.cpp ${SLICE_SWEEP2_OV047_SOURCES})

#     from:0x021130ec kind:load to:0x0211442c module:overlay(22)

#   both under the right names (ov022_syms.txt:171 and :187).

#   than carried: 0x02114690's other reference is at 0x02112914, inside

#     from:0x021126fc kind:arm_call to:0x02112654 module:overlay(22)
# 0x02112654 is func_ov022_02112654, on this lane's slice. No mount defines

#
# W3, THE TWO CleanupResources BODIES THAT SPELL THEIR SharedFilePtrs G0/G1.
# hal/cxx_aliases.cpp binds _G0 to the game heap pointer and _G1 to SignPost's
# ov002 collision file, so linking either of these as written would Release a
# live pointer on every level-14 teardown -- the failure that made wave 8 host
# -thunk LAVA_PLANK's slot 3. Each pool says what its two really are, and both
# are already in port/ov022_syms.txt:
#   73  _ZN16daObjFl_London_c16CleanupResourcesEv: 0x02111aa0 -> 0x02114580, 0x02111aa4 -> 0x02114578
#   77  _ZN10LavaSeesaw16CleanupResourcesEv: 0x02111dcc -> 0x021145a8, 0x02111dd0 -> 0x021145a0
# (Both files are .c, so both names carry C linkage and bind straight onto the
# mount's plain C symbols -- no decorated-name bridge is needed here.)
# BOTH W3 RENAMES RETIRED at the SYNC6 main -> port sync, and the first one had
# become a defect rather than a fix. main's consolidation gave both TUs the real
# symbols in their own text -- src/actors/daObjFl_London_c.cpp lines 46-47 spell
# `extern void *data_ov022_02114580;` and `extern void *data_ov022_02114578;`
# themselves, and neither file contains the identifiers G0 or G1 any more (grep,
# on the merged tree) -- so there is nothing left for a -D to rewrite.
#
# The harm: include/decl_common.h(394) declares `extern int G1[];` for a
# different symbol entirely, and a -D rewrites THAT declaration too, in every
# TU it is applied to. So the London TU compiled decl_common's line as
# `extern int data_ov022_02114578[];` and then met its own
# `extern void *data_ov022_02114578;` eleven lines later:
#
#   src/actors/daObjFl_London_c.cpp(47): error C2372: 'data_ov022_02114578':
#   redefinition; different types of indirection
#   include/decl_common.h(394): note: see declaration of 'data_ov022_02114578'
#
# That is the C2372 lane SYNC5 quarantined this TU for and lane FACES2 recorded
# as a decomp-side question ("which spelling is right is a ROM question").  It
# is neither: it is this rename, firing on a header declaration it was never
# meant to see. The LavaSeesaw row goes with it for the same reason -- unused,
# and the same latent collision on decl_common's G1.
#
# The pool derivations above stay as the record of what the two words are.
#
# W4, THE SAME FIX DOES NOT RETIRE WAVE 8's ONE HOST THUNK, AND THE REFUSAL IS
# MEASURED. LAVA_PLANK (82)'s slot 3,
# src/_ZN9LavaPlank16CleanupResourcesEv.cpp, is the third body of
# exactly this shape, and the rename is KNOWN: its pool reads
# 0x02112208 -> 0x02114620 and 0x0211220c -> 0x02114618, both
# module:overlay(22) and both already mounted. It still cannot be used. This
# body's two targets are declared in include/decl_common.h (lines 238-239,
# `extern char data_ov022_02114618[]` and `..._02114620[]`) and so is G1 (line
# 396, `extern int G1[]`), so -DG1=data_ov022_02114618 rewrites one into a
# redefinition of the other with a different type. MEASURED, not predicted:
# error C2371 on decl_common.h(396) and on the .cpp's own line 9. That is the
# ov006 Mg3DEsp wall recorded at line ~6295 of this file, and the test that
# separates the two cases is whether the TARGET is in that header --
# 0x02114580, 0x02114578, 0x021145a8 and 0x021145a0 are not, which is exactly
# why W3 above works. hal/actor_classes_ov022.cpp therefore KEEPS lp_clean and

# HOST-ABI RETIREMENT: Player::InitResources, the host copy that existed only

# codegen shape (5 x 4 strb post-inc), not to compute anything, and what it
# computes is a 20-byte zero over a fresh allocation. hostgen's ASM_EXCISION

# shape. The matched TU spells `unsigned char data_02092660;` inside extern
# "C", a strong definition to MSVC's C++ front end, and the byte is DS state
# hal/scene_boot.cpp owns inside the .dsstate bracket (dsstate_guard refuses
# it anywhere else). --extern-data turns that one line into a declaration and
# the body links as it stands. port/unmatched/Scene_AfterCleanupResources.cpp
# used to be the matched source with that one word added; it is deleted.
set(HOSTABI_RETIRE_SYMS _ZN6Player13InitResourcesEv
    _ZN8dScene_c21AfterCleanupResourcesEj)

# run mg9 lane S364: dScMgSlot1_c, actor id 0x16c = scene 364. The ROM gives
# this id no Mg*_SpawnInfo symbol and no naming import has ever named it, so
# the class name is the ROM's own RTTI, reached through the type_info the word
# BEFORE the vtable points at: data_ov006_0213eb40[-1] is 0x0213e5a0, whose
# name pointer 0x0213e5bc reads "12dScMgSlot1_c".
#
# THE WIDTH IS THE REASON THIS BLOCK IS WORTH READING. port/mg_fanout_costs.txt
# section 11 names 0x16c by hand as the second class whose phantom slot 36 is
# LIVE DATA BELONGING TO A SHIPPED GAME: index 36 of this table is
# g_profile_MG_SMARTBALL's factory word, and scene 376 is seated in
# this tree. hal/scene_mg_slot1.cpp fills 36 and port/slice_s364.txt section 3
# carries all four checks -- span, terminal slot, what the word is, and the
# relocation count.
#
# ONE VARIABLE FOR THE SLICE, for the reason the CCN and PPP blocks state.
# hal/scene_boot.cpp's port_scene_classes table carries the scene-364 row, so
# every target that compiles scene_boot.cpp references port_mg_slot1_spawn and
# port_scene_fill_slot1 by name -- the same coupling every minigame row has.
#
# NO STATE DISPATCHER HOST COPY AND NO stategen OUTPUT. This class has no mwcc
# pointer-to-member state machine: its own machine is a fourteen-arm jump-table
# switch, no overlay constructor builds a pair table for it, and a `::*` sweep
# over every TU in the slice is clean. That is the second counterexample to
# section 4's "the wall is the same one for all thirty", after the flower.
#
# ONE TU BUILDS FROM A HOSTGEN COPY. src/_ZN12dScMgSlot1_c13InitResourcesEv.cpp is slot 0,
# InitResources, and it does thirty-seven literal-address accesses in the
# 0x04xxxxxx window -- both engines' DISPCNT and BGxCNT at 0x0400000c /
# 0x0400000e / 0x04001008 / 0x0400100a / 0x0400100c / 0x0400100e, BLDCNT at
# 0x04000050 and the sub-engine blend at 0x04001050. Compiled straight from
# src/ those land in the memory ntr maps across the I/O window and stop there.
# src/ itself is never edited; the hostgen copy stands in for it and the
# substitution asserts rather than hopes, exactly as the FLW block's does.
set(S364_HOSTGEN_SYMS _ZN12dScMgSlot1_c13InitResourcesEv)
set(S364_HOSTGEN_GEN "")
set(S364_HOSTGEN_SKIP "")
foreach(sym IN LISTS S364_HOSTGEN_SYMS)
    if(EXISTS "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/${sym}.c")
        set(sym_src "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/${sym}.c")
        list(APPEND S364_HOSTGEN_SKIP "src/${sym}.c")
    else()
        set(sym_src "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/${sym}.cpp")
        list(APPEND S364_HOSTGEN_SKIP "src/${sym}.cpp")
    endif()
    set(sym_out "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src/src/${sym}.cpp")
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT "${sym_out}"
        COMMAND python "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/hostgen.py"
                --out "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src" ${sym}
        DEPENDS "${sym_src}" "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/hostgen.py"
        COMMENT "hostgen ${sym}")
    list(APPEND S364_HOSTGEN_GEN "${sym_out}")
endforeach()

port_read_lines("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/slice_s364.txt" SLICE_S364_LINES)
set(SLICE_S364_SOURCES ${S364_HOSTGEN_GEN})
foreach(line IN LISTS SLICE_S364_LINES)
    string(STRIP "${line}" line)
    if(line MATCHES "^#" OR line STREQUAL "")
        continue()
    endif()
    # The hostgen'd copy stands in for the src/ one; taking both would be a
    # duplicate symbol, and taking neither would drop the body silently.
    if(line IN_LIST S364_HOSTGEN_SKIP)
        continue()
    endif()
    list(APPEND SLICE_S364_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../${line}")
endforeach()
list(LENGTH S364_HOSTGEN_SYMS s364_hg_want)
list(LENGTH S364_HOSTGEN_GEN s364_hg_have)
if(NOT s364_hg_want EQUAL s364_hg_have)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "slice_s364 hostgen substitution incomplete: "
            "${s364_hg_have} of ${s364_hg_want} generated")
endif()
foreach(skip IN LISTS S364_HOSTGEN_SKIP)
    if(NOT skip IN_LIST SLICE_S364_LINES)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "slice_s364.txt no longer lists ${skip}; the "
                "hostgen substitution for it is now dead and the display "
                "control writes in it would go back to latching silently")
    endif()
endforeach()

# TWO NAME-SPELLING DEFECTS, BOTH SECTION 6's FOURTH KIND, BOTH RESOLVED OFF
# THE ROM RATHER THAN OFF THE NAME. The first link wave asked for seven
# externals and all seven are decomp-side spellings of DATA symbols under a
# func_ prefix. Per-source -D and not /alternatename, for lane A2's reason: the
# right-hand symbols are DEFINED in this binary by the ov004 mount, and an
# alias with a defined symbol on the left is defeated silently.
#
# (a) THE SIX ov004 WINDOW WORDS slot 0 writes -- 0x80, 0x40, 0x80, 0x40, 0x80,
#     0x40 into 0x020bc88c, _020bc860, _020bc878, _020bc890, _020bc8b8 and
#     _020bc8b4. include/decl_common.h declares all six as `extern int
#     func_020bcXXX;`, config names every one of them data_ov004_020bcXXX at
#     four bytes each, and port/ov004_syms.txt already mounts the whole run.
#     port/mg_fanout_costs.txt section 12 records dScMgCup_c's InitResources
#     writing "the six ov004 window words" as well, so this rename is the
#     family's and not this class's.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src/src/_ZN12dScMgSlot1_c13InitResourcesEv.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
    "func_020bc860=data_ov004_020bc860;func_020bc878=data_ov004_020bc878;func_020bc88c=data_ov004_020bc88c;func_020bc890=data_ov004_020bc890;func_020bc8b4=data_ov004_020bc8b4;func_020bc8b8=data_ov004_020bc8b8")

# (b) THE SUB-OBJECT'S BASE VTABLE, and this one had to be ADJUDICATED BETWEEN
#     TWO OVERLAYS rather than looked up. The factory and both destructors
#     store 0x020ad494 into this+0x4660 and then store the betIcon table over
#     it -- a base-then-derived vptr pair. 0x020ad494 is `ambiguous` in config:
#     ov000 and ov001 share the base 0x020aa420 and both name a symbol there.
#     hal/scene_mg_faces.cpp already hosts the ov000 reading, a 24-byte
#     filename string "thum_shinkei_ncg.bin", AND THAT IS THE WRONG MODULE FOR
#     THIS CLASS. The ROM decides it:
#
#       overlay_0001.bin at 0x020ad478 is a type_info record {0x0209a774,
#       0x020ad480} and 0x020ad480 reads "9dThIcon_c";
#       0x020ad490 holds 0x020ad478, i.e. that type_info, which is the word
#       before a vtable;
#       0x020ad494 and 0x020ad498 hold 0x020ab550 and 0x020ab54c, a two-slot
#       table -- and src/_ZN12dScMgSlot1_c9betIcon_c8BehaviorEv.cpp, the DERIVED betIcon slot 0,
#       calls _ZN9dThIcon_c8BehaviorEv directly, which is the base calling
#       convention showing through;
#       overlay_0000.bin at the same address is the middle of the string
#       "...ogezo/togezo.bmd", which is not a type_info and not a table.
#
#     So dScMgSlot1_c::betIcon_c derives from dThIcon_c in ov001. The ov001
#     per-symbol mount covers 0x020ab800..0x020abb00 only (port/ov001_syms.txt
#     says why), so the table is HOSTED in hal/scene_mg_slot1.cpp with faces
#     for its two ROM bodies rather than mounted, which is the same treatment
#     and the same reasoning hal/scene_mg_faces.cpp gives for the ov000
#     reading of this very address. Expanding the ov001 mount instead would be
#     the wrong trade for two words and would put a raw DS code address in the
#     table anyway.
foreach(s364_thicon_tu
        "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/_ZN12dScMgSlot1_cD1Ev.cpp"
        "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/_ZN12dScMgSlot1_cD0Ev.cpp"
        "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}/src/d_s_mg_slot1.cpp")
    set_source_files_properties("${s364_thicon_tu}"
        PROPERTIES COMPILE_DEFINITIONS
        "func_020ad494=data_ov001_020ad494")
endforeach()

set(SCENE_MG_SLOT1_SOURCES hal/scene_mg_slot1.cpp)

# Run mg11 lane MUG: dScMgSlot3_c, the "Mix-a-Mug" slot machine, actor id
# 0x16d = scene 365, and the NINTH class the port seats under
# dScMgSingle3DBase_c (eight at base; port/slice_mug.txt has the sweep that
# counts them).
#
#   Scene -> dScMgBase_c (ov004 0x020bc0c0) -> dScMgSingle3DBase_c
#         (ov006 0x0213e448) -> dScMgSlot3_c (ov006 0x0213eaa8)
#
# both new tables 36 slots wide and checked FIVE ways before a word was written
# (port/slice_mug.txt): the span, the terminal slot, what the words past the
# end are, the relocation count inside the span, and the relocation stride.
# THE SPAN READS 38 AND THE WIDTH IS 36, which port/mg_fanout_costs.txt line
# 1287 already resolved; what the slice adds is the mechanism, and it names a
# live victim -- the two extra words are the {0, &typeinfo} RTTI HEADER of
# dScMgSlot1_c's vtable, so a 38-slot fill here would write a host thunk over
# scene 364's typeinfo pointer. The ROM gives this id no spawn symbol at all,
# so the whole identity -- class name, hierarchy and player title -- is derived
# from the ROM in that file's header.
#
# THE WALL IS THE ORDINARY TABLE FORM AND IT IS PAID ONCE. Eight states in
# data_ov006_02142bdc, filled by __sinit_ov006_02132894 and dispatched from
# vtable slot 6 at stride eight with arity 0. unmatched/MgSlot3_StateDispatch.cpp
# host-copies _ZN12dScMgSlot3_c8BehaviorEv and routes the dispatch through an address
# switch, so src/_ZN12dScMgSlot3_c8BehaviorEv.cpp is OUT of slice_mug.txt: listing both
# copies would be a duplicate symbol, and listing neither would drop the whole
# state machine silently. A word-by-word decode of the class's code block finds
# exactly THREE Itanium-sequence instructions and all three are in that one
# body, so there is no second dispatcher and no open-coded third shape.
#
# THE ONE BODILESS STATE IS RETIRED (run mg12, lane MAM). func_ov006_0210adac
# (slot 2, 0x1b8, the face-evaluation step after the third reel stops) had a
# config symbol, no delink block and no src in any module, so mg11 left it out
# of the slice and invented no definition for it. It is now byte-matched:
# src/func_ov006_0210adac.c is in slice_mug.txt, the delink block covers
# 0x0210adac..0x0210af64, and unmatched/MgSlot3_StateDispatch.cpp calls it. The
# per-slot census still prints the former floor counter so an mg11 log and an
# mg12 log compare field for field.
#
# NO HOSTGEN SUBSTITUTION, for the reason the S381 block above gives: the two
# bodies in this class that dereference a 0x04xxxxxx literal
# (src/_ZN12dScMgSlot3_c13InitResourcesEv.cpp's BG0CNT/BG1CNT/BG2CNT/BG3CNT writes and
# src/_ZN12dScMgSlot3_c9Virtual80Ev.cpp's BG1CNT read-modify-writes) are ordinary PPU
# control registers the display reads back out of the memory ntr maps there.
# The write-TRIGGERED registers this class touches are all inside
# _ZN19dScMgSingle3DBase_c9Virtual84Ev, which comes in through FLW_HOSTGEN_GEN already
# substituted.
#
# ONE VARIABLE, for the reason the flower and S381 blocks give: the slice and
# the .cpp are not separable. hal/scene_boot.cpp's port_scene_classes table
# carries the scene-365 row, so every target that compiles scene_boot.cpp
# references port_mg_slot3_spawn and port_scene_fill_slot3 by name.
port_read_lines("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/slice_mug.txt" SLICE_MUG_LINES)
set(SLICE_MUG_SOURCES hal/scene_mg_slot3.cpp
                      unmatched/MgSlot3_StateDispatch.cpp)
# unmatched/MgSlot3_SubObjCtor.cpp RETIRED (run linkfull, lane RS4PORT): main
# #3107 spells the two file ids 0x205/0x206, so src/func_ov006_020c221c.c is
# on slice_mug.txt.
# unmatched/MgSlot3_SubObjUpdate_020c1f4c.cpp RETIRED (run link100, lane
# FOLD2): its shadow's v3() is ROM index 3, BlendModelAnim::UpdateVerts, which
# is what _ZTV14BlendModelAnim[3] holds again. src/func_ov006_020c1f4c.cpp
# carries it (port/slice_fold2.txt).
foreach(line IN LISTS SLICE_MUG_LINES)
    string(STRIP "${line}" line)
    if(line MATCHES "^#" OR line STREQUAL "")
        continue()
    endif()
    list(APPEND SLICE_MUG_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../${line}")
endforeach()

# Run mg11 lane RLT: dScMgRoulette_c, actor id 0x17f = scene 383, "Mushroom
# Roulette", and the FIFTH class the port seats under dScMgSingle3DBase_c.
#
#   Scene -> dScMgBase_c (ov004 0x020bc0c0) -> dScMgSingle3DBase_c
#         (ov006 0x0213e448) -> dScMgRoulette_c (ov006 0x0213e39c)
#
# both new tables 36 slots wide and checked FOUR ways before a word was written
# (port/slice_rlt.txt): span, terminal slot, what the word past the end is, and
# the relocation count inside the span with no row at index 36. The class name
# is the ROM's own type_info, "15dScMgRoulette_c" at 0x0213e30c, reached through
# the relocation the word before the vtable carries.
#
# THREE HOST COPIES, AND EACH IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT:
#
#   MgRoulette_Factory.cpp        REPLACES src/dScMgRoulette_c_classInit.cpp. The
#     SECOND AND LAST factory in the family that calls _ZN11dScMgBase_cC2Ev with
#     no argument -- port/unmatched/MgCup_Factory.cpp names this exact TU as the
#     other one. On ARM r0 still holds the object after `movs r4,r0`; on the
#     host the callee reads [esp+4] and writes three vtable words through it.
#     The displacement ruling is port/mg_fanout_costs.txt section 12's, spent
#     here for the other id that paragraph names.
#   MgRoulette_WheelDispatch.cpp  REPLACES src/actors/dScMgRoulette_c.cpp, which
#     carries TWO defects in eleven lines: the class's ONE mwcc member-pointer
#     dispatch (pair at offset 0 of the wheel object at +0x530c, universe of
#     exactly two code words bounded from the relocation set) and a local
#     shadow-class call of ROM vtable slot 3 on a HOST Model.
#   MgRoulette_ModelRender_02107d80.cpp  REPLACES src/actors/dScMgRoulette_c.cpp,
#     the same shadow defect at ROM slot 5, twice, on the DRAW path. A separate
#     file because the two failures look nothing alike and only one of them is
#     what a rendered frame depends on.
#
# All three src TUs are therefore OUT of port/slice_rlt.txt; listing both copies
# would be an LNK2005 and listing neither would drop the body silently. The
# assertion below is here rather than at the link because a duplicate-symbol
# wall reports far from its cause.
#
# NO LANGUAGE CXX ROW AND NO PER-SOURCE -D ROW, and both are sweeps rather than
# absences. All 41 TUs in the class's code block were scanned for the //cpp
# marker and for extern "C", virtual, class and namespace before the first
# build: the six hits are all already .cpp files (02107920, 02107a6c, 02107d80,
# 02107db8, 0210a194 and the factory), so CMake compiles each as C++ on its
# extension and no .c path in this slice is really C++. A scan of every source
# this seat adds for the bare placeholders VT, VT0, HEAP, G0, G1, G2, R0, R1 and
# R2 returns nothing.
#
# NO HOSTGEN SUBSTITUTION EITHER, and it is a decision rather than an omission,
# the same one the S381 block above records. The one body of this class's chain
# that writes a WRITE-TRIGGERED register is _ZN19dScMgSingle3DBase_c9Virtual84Ev (slot 33,
# LIGHT_COLOR at 0x040004cc), and that comes in already substituted through
# FLW_HOSTGEN_GEN. Slot 0's own writes -- 0x0400100c, 0x04001008 and 0x04000008
# -- are ordinary PPU control registers the display reads back out of the memory
# ntr maps there.
#
# ONE VARIABLE, for the reason the flower, fader and S381 blocks give: the slice
# and the .cpp are not separable. hal/scene_boot.cpp's port_scene_classes table
# now carries the scene-383 row, so every target that compiles scene_boot.cpp
# references port_mg_roulette_spawn and port_scene_fill_roulette by name.
#
# THE SLICE IS THE DELTA ONLY. slice_mg1.txt carries the ov004 framework, the
# thirty-five overlay constructors and the arm9 waves under them; slice_mem.txt
# carries the +0x4f38 model sub-object family this class shares with
# dScMgMemory2_c (including MgMemory2_FieldPmf.cpp, which routes the field
# member pointer this class's slot 6 dispatches every frame); slice_flw.txt and
# slice_mga361.txt carry the eight dScMgSingle3DBase_c bodies. CMake appends
# every list to the same targets and dedupes identical absolute paths, so
# nothing is compiled twice.
port_read_lines("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/slice_rlt.txt" SLICE_RLT_LINES)
set(SLICE_RLT_SOURCES hal/scene_mg_roulette.cpp
                      unmatched/MgRoulette_Factory.cpp
                      unmatched/MgRoulette_WheelDispatch.cpp)
# unmatched/MgRoulette_ModelRender_02107d80.cpp RETIRED (run link100, lane

# (port/slice_fold2.txt).

    string(STRIP "${line}" line)
    if(line MATCHES "^#" OR line STREQUAL "")
        continue()
    endif()
    list(APPEND SLICE_RLT_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../${line}")
endforeach()
foreach(dup IN ITEMS src/minigames/d_s_mg_roulette.cpp src/actors/dScMgRoulette_c.cpp

    if(dup IN_LIST SLICE_RLT_LINES)

            "slice_rlt.txt lists ${dup}, which port/unmatched/ host-copies. "

    endif()

# The per-source vtable-store bindings. Each _Spawn/dtor stores its object's
# vptr through recovered names (VT0/VT1/VT2 and _ZTV<recovered>) whose ADDRESS
# is per source: the SAME recovered name is a different table in a different TU
# (_ZTV15daObjWc_Obj07_c is 0x021091d4 in daObjWc_Obj07_c_classInit but the own
# table 0x02114018 in the RectangleD1 TU -- the ov065 disease). Read off each
# body's own literal pool. Rule applied: the LIVE (last) store gets its true
# target (the own host array for a spawn; _ZTV10dBgActor_c for a destructor, the
# base reached at the bottom of the dtor chain); every DEAD earlier store is
# pointed at a guaranteed-defined host symbol (the class's own array), because
# it is immediately overwritten and its value never reaches a virtual call. The
# ROM's own ov002 base tables (_ZTV17daObjFloatBoard_c/021091d4) are NOT host arrays,
# so a dead store is never bound to them.
#
# Spawns -- live store is the own table:
# lane CDEFS 2026-09-16: a dead COMPILE_DEFINITIONS row stood here.
# A LATER set_source_files_properties() names d_a_obj_wc_obj01.cpp for the same
# property, and that call REPLACES this one, so nothing on this row ever
# reached the compiler. Each definition it carried, against the synced TU:
#   _ZTV14daObjWcObj01_c=_ZTV14daObjWcObj01_c  --  identity rename, a no-op even if it had run
#   VT1=_ZTV14daObjWcObj01_c  --  dead, the TU does not spell VT1
# Deleted rather than merged. The surviving row is unchanged.
# lane CDEFS 2026-09-16: a dead COMPILE_DEFINITIONS row stood here.
# A LATER set_source_files_properties() names d_a_obj_wc_obj06.cpp for the same
# property, and that call REPLACES this one, so nothing on this row ever
# reached the compiler. Each definition it carried, against the synced TU:
#   _ZTV14daObjWcObj06_c=_ZTV14daObjWcObj06_c  --  identity rename, a no-op even if it had run
#   VT1=_ZTV14daObjWcObj06_c  --  dead, the TU does not spell VT1
# Deleted rather than merged. The surviving row is unchanged.
# lane CDEFS 2026-09-16: a dead COMPILE_DEFINITIONS row stood here.
# A LATER set_source_files_properties() names d_a_obj_wc_obj07.cpp for the same
# property, and that call REPLACES this one, so nothing on this row ever
# reached the compiler. Each definition it carried, against the synced TU:
#   _ZTV15daObjWc_Obj07_c=_ZTV15daObjWc_Obj07_c  --  identity rename, a no-op even if it had run
#   VT1=_ZTV15daObjWc_Obj07_c  --  dead, the TU does not spell VT1
# Deleted rather than merged. The surviving row is unchanged.
# (ArrowLift/WaterDiamond/CageLift/SwitchActivatedPlank/WDW_Water spawns store
#  their own already-defined host symbol and need no binding.)
#
# Destructors -- live (last) store is _ZTV10dBgActor_c; dead stores to the own array:
# lane CDEFS 2026-09-16: a dead COMPILE_DEFINITIONS row stood here.
# A LATER set_source_files_properties() names d_a_obj_wc_obj01.cpp for the same
# property, and that call REPLACES this one, so nothing on this row ever
# reached the compiler. Each definition it carried, against the synced TU:
#   _ZTV14daObjWcObj01_c=_ZTV14daObjWcObj01_c  --  identity rename, a no-op even if it had run
#   _ZTV10dBgActor_c=_ZTV14daObjWcObj01_c  --  dead, the TU does not spell _ZTV10dBgActor_c
#   VT2=_ZTV10dBgActor_c  --  dead, the TU does not spell VT2
# Deleted rather than merged. The surviving row is unchanged.
# GATE 229 CORRECTION (lane SEAT3). This row predates any seat of the TU, so it
# was never compiled and never checked. VT1 read the class's OWN table where the
# body's literal pool at 0x02111248 holds the ov002 base 0x02108fdc, and G0 was
# missing entirely, which would have left `extern void *G0;` unresolved. Both
# fixed from config/arm9/overlays/ov029/relocs.txt inside the body's own span.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/game/actors/d_a_obj_wc_obj01.cpp"

    # compiles.

# run linkw wave 8 (lane w8-a): THE STAGE CLASS CLOSURE, first landed piece.
#
# Eight matched Stage bodies plus the one callee they drag (nine TUs), the
# class's own arm9 BSS (hal/w8a_stage_storage.cpp) and the C-name faces that
# reach them (hal/w8a_stage_faces.cpp). There are no /include: link roots here
# and NOTHING REACHES THESE YET: every one of the nine is /OPT:REF-stripped and
# every alias LHS is unused, which is why this lands at the linkage floor. The
# slice head records, per held-out TU, the measured blocker that keeps the other
# twenty-one out; the faces file records that the reach does not exist, because
# the ROM reaches all of these through _ZTV5Stage, which hal/stage_bridges.cpp
# still trap-fills. Seating that table is what turns this groundwork live.
port_read_lines("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/slice_w8a.txt" SLICE_W8A_LINES)
set(SLICE_W8A_SOURCES "")
foreach(line IN LISTS SLICE_W8A_LINES)
    string(STRIP "${line}" line)
    if(line MATCHES "^#" OR line STREQUAL "")
        continue()
    endif()
    list(APPEND SLICE_W8A_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../${line}")
endforeach()

# Gate 12: the interactive window (same stack, windowed loop).
#
# tests/io_pressure.cpp is the negative control for ntr/io.cpp's fixed-address
# reservation: it takes 0x02000000 before the game asks for it, so the failure a
# player hit can be reproduced on demand against THIS binary rather than against
# a special build of it. Inert unless SM64DS_IO_PRESSURE_AT is set in the
# environment, and nothing in the tree sets it.

add_executable(walk_window tests/walk_window.cpp tests/io_pressure.cpp "${OV002DATA_C}" ${LEVEL_OV_DATA}
    # run link100 lane BOOT: the ROM's own boot chain, called from the four
    # port_boot_rom_* seams in tests/walk_window.cpp's main. See the gate-214
    # block above and the header of hal/boot_os.cpp.
    ${SLICE214_SOURCES} ${SLICE_IPCSEND_SOURCES}
    # dialogue pipeline (2026-08-08): the box pump (Stage::UpdateMessage's
    # dialogue arm), the engine-A 2D-over-3D compositor, and the headless probe.
    hal/message_pump.cpp hal/message_compositor.cpp hal/message_probe.cpp hal/message_gen_text.cpp hal/input_probe.cpp
    # the launcher's settings.json, read by the game (camera turn direction,
    # and the four screen-gap keys hal/screen_gap.cpp reads)
    hal/host_settings.cpp hal/screen_gap.cpp
    # run perf1: the player performance log, playlog/perf-<id>.jsonl beside the
    # flight recorder. A second reader of what the F3 overlay already measures,
    # so it adds no measurement path and no picture; the frame pump hands it
    # one struct a frame and it writes one line every five seconds. Every
    # hardware string it names is reached through LoadLibraryA/GetProcAddress
    # or the CPUID instruction, so the import table does not move -- the same
    # rule the two graphics-card files below keep.
    hal/perf_log.cpp
    # the controller backend: XInput slots 0..3, then a DirectInput pad
    # (Switch Pro, DualShock, DualSense, generic HID) mapped onto the XInput
    # mask. Both DLLs loaded dynamically; no xinput/dinput8/dxguid lib. On
    # both targets that compile tests/walk_window.cpp, which is its caller.
    hal/pad_backend.cpp
    # run hd2 lane GPU1: the optional Direct3D 11 present path. Off by default
    # and inert when off: with PresentBackend absent or 0 it loads nothing,
    # creates nothing and prints nothing. d3d11 is LoadLibrary'd and its one
    # entry point GetProcAddress'd, the same rule hal/pad_backend.cpp keeps
    # above, so no d3d11, dxgi or dxguid lib is linked and the exe's import
    # table does not move. Its shaders are compiled offline into
    # hal/gpu_present_shaders.h, so d3dcompiler never loads either. On both
    # targets that compile tests/walk_window.cpp, which is its caller.
    hal/gpu_present.cpp
    # run hd2 lane GPU2: the ONE Direct3D 11 device this process makes. It
    # exists because a second optional setting is about to want a device and
    # two devices would be two copies of every texture on the card and two
    # claims on a 32-bit process's address space, which the stage-0 probe
    # measured as the tightest resource here. Nothing asks it for a device
    # unless a setting that needs one is on, so with every key absent it loads
    # nothing and allocates nothing. Same LoadLibrary rule as the file above:
    # no d3d11, dxgi or dxguid lib is linked and the import table does not move.
    hal/gpu_device.cpp
    # run hd2 lane GPU2: the optional renderer that draws the opaque 3D pass
    # on that device. Off by default and inert when off: with Renderer absent
    # or 0 it registers no backend, asks for no device and allocates nothing.
    # Its shaders are compiled offline into hal/gpu_raster_shaders.h, same as
    # the present path's, so d3dcompiler never loads here either.
    hal/gpu_raster.cpp
    # run lvled lane B: the editor control channel on 127.0.0.1:7355, the link
    # the Studio's editor talks to. Compiled in unconditionally but INERT unless
    # SM64DS_EDITOR_CHANNEL=1 -- no thread, no socket, no listener without it.
    # It is on BOTH targets that compile tests/walk_window.cpp (walk_window and
    # walk_window_hires), because the frame loop's drain call lives in that
    # shared file and a target without this source fails the link.
    hal/editor_channel.cpp
    # run lvled lane g3: live skybox switching for the editor's `skyset` verb.
    # Same story as the channel and the same flag: compiled in unconditionally,
    # INERT until editor_channel_init calls port_editor_sky_arm(), which it
    # does only under SM64DS_EDITOR_CHANNEL=1. Unarmed it runs no line,
    # allocates nothing and writes no game state, which is what lets the
    # battery -- which runs unarmed -- stand as the proof that it changed
    # nothing. On both walk_window targets for the channel's reason.
    hal/editor_sky.cpp
    # the Mods panel's file-layer half: installs hal/fs.cpp's mod hooks
    # (LovesMeCharacter). Game-shaped targets only; every smoke keeps the
    # null hooks and stock file serving.
    hal/fs_mods.cpp
    # SM64DS_STAGE_GEOM: a level's stage model and collision served out of an

    # the scene's hand-drawn gap band and the band's per-scene continuity

    # in-memory save state (lane lk6): F8/F9 snapshot and restore of the hosted

    hal/clsn_vtable.cpp hal/actor_vtables.cpp hal/anim_bridge.cpp
    ${SLICE_W8SHADOWS_SOURCES}
    # hal/megachar_stub.cpp is NOT here any more (lane w8-shadows). Its
    # `return 0` stand-in for Platform::UpdateKillByMegaChar is now compiled
    # only into the three narrow gate-9 harnesses above, which cannot build the
    # real closure. In this target the ROM's C name is the face at the bottom
    # of hal/wf_enemy_bridges.cpp and the body is the matched TU that has been

# The runtime-selectable 16:9 layer. Off (the default) it renders the 512x384
# 4:3 window ZOOM 2 the port has always shipped -- the software raster is
# fill-bound and 2x is ~12ms -> 60fps; on it renders the full 1024x576 16:9. One
# exe, the Aspect settings key (a ratio, 0 = native) picks it at boot. Was ntr_2x
# (NTR_HIRES2, the fixed 512x384 tier); the wide-max buffer with a 4:3 default
# active size is byte-for-byte that build when the key is off.
target_link_libraries(walk_window PRIVATE ntr_wide_rt)
target_compile_definitions(walk_window PRIVATE SM64DS_PLATFORM_PC
    ${PORT_REPO_ROOT_DEF}
    # GATE STARSEL (run link100, lane STARSELENTRY): this target carries
    # hal/input_probe.cpp, so hal/scene_boot.cpp's port_scene_tick can call
    # port_input_probe_apply.  smoke_player does not compile input_probe.cpp
    # (see its own source list), so the call there stays guarded off.
    SM64DS_SCENE_PAD_PROBE=1
    # GATE 220 (run link100, lane FRAME): this target carries
    # port/slice_gate220.txt and hal/stage_frame.cpp, so _ZTV5Stage
    # slot 6 dispatches the ROM's own Stage::Behavior instead of the
    # host occupant.  smoke_player does not define this and keeps the
    # occupant; see the gate row above it for why.
    SM64DS_STAGE_SLOT6_ROM=1
    # GATE SLOT9 (run link100, lane RENDER9): the same for slot 9 and
    # Stage::Render.  SM64DS_STAGE_SLOT9_HOST=1 in the ENVIRONMENT makes the
    # seated thunk decline at run time, which is how the BMP A/B is captured
    # on ONE binary; the compile definition is what puts the ROM body in the
    # slot at all.
    SM64DS_STAGE_SLOT9_ROM=1
    # GATE SHADOWS RUNG 3 (run link100, lane SHADOWS2): this target carries
    # port/slice_shadows.txt AND port/slice_gate16.txt, so the ROM's own
    # SharedFilePtr::ReallocateModelFile is in the link with func_02017060
    # under it.  The define retires the empty stand-in in
    # hal/gx_upload_bridge.cpp, which would otherwise defeat that file's
    # /alternatename by defining its LHS.  The ten narrow harnesses link the
    # caller without the callee and keep the stand-in.
    SM64DS_SFP_REALLOC_ROM=1
    # this target links hal/cxx_aliases.cpp, which already carries
    # the Heap::_Deallocate face hal/blend_vtable.cpp repeats
    PORT_CXX_ALIASES_LINKED)
# ROM-CLEAN: the shipped window loads its ROM tables from romdata.bin at boot.
# The dispatch (generated) + loader come in as extra sources, PORT_ROM_CLEAN
# turns on the port_romdata_load() call in walk_window.cpp, and a custom target
# makes the blob + self-check a build prerequisite.
if(PORT_ROM_CLEAN)
    # hal/asset_root_refuse.cpp: the shipping build has NO PORT_REPO_ROOT
    # fallback for assets. It is in this block and only this block, so the
    # developer build keeps the fallback every lane in this tree relies on.
    # Run link60 lane KIT1; port/kit_pipeline.txt is the write-up.
    target_sources(walk_window PRIVATE "${ROMDATA_DISPATCH_C}"
                   hal/romdata_loader.cpp hal/asset_root_refuse.cpp)
    target_compile_definitions(walk_window PRIVATE PORT_ROM_CLEAN)
    add_custom_target(romblob_ready_ww DEPENDS "${ROMDATA_BIN}"
        "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/assets/romblob_verified.stamp"
        "${ROMDATA_RECIPE}")
    add_dependencies(walk_window romblob_ready_ww)
endif()
if(MSVC)
    target_compile_options(walk_window PRIVATE /wd4311 /wd4312 /wd4068 /wd4576)
    # No ASLR for the shipped window: a disk save state (hal/lk7_persist
    # .cpp) stores absolute pointers into the exe image -- every actor's
    # vtable pointer -- and they only relocate if the image loads at the
    # SAME base on the next launch. ASLR rebases once per boot, which
    # would refuse every state written before a reboot. The header still
    # checks the base, so if anything rebases the exe anyway the state is
    # refused with a message rather than loaded onto dangling pointers.
    target_link_options(walk_window PRIVATE /DYNAMICBASE:NO)
endif()

# The save state captures the whole .dsstate section (hal/dsstate_seg.h). Fail
# the build if a hosted DS global landed OUTSIDE it: that symbol would not roll
# back on a restore, which is exactly the class of bug that shipped in 0.2.0
# (the ANIM_PTRS table crashing Player::SetAnim on a null BCA_File*). The map
# the guard reads is the one /MAP already writes next to the exe.
add_custom_command(TARGET walk_window POST_BUILD
    COMMAND python "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/dsstate_guard.py"
            "$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:walk_window>/walk_window.map"
    VERBATIM
    COMMENT "dsstate_guard: hosted DS globals all inside .dsstate")

# A FACE MUST NEVER FORWARD TO ANOTHER FACE. The port reaches the ROM's code
# through one-line forwarders, and each shape rests on a premise about the other
# side: the flat-name face assumes the member is a real body, the member face
# assumes the flat name is. Nothing checked either premise, so two faces written
# against each other -- in two files, by two people, months apart -- resolve
# cleanly, duplicate nothing, leave nothing unresolved, pass every static gate,
# and then call themselves forever. SYNC6 caught the LOUD version of this, where
# a translation unit came back and the generated forwarder became a second
# definition and the linker said LNK2005. The silent version has no such signal,
# and on 2026-09-14 the shipped artifact carried eight of them; the first one to
# run took the whole process down with a stack overflow on level 28's first
# frame. This guard reads the map and the image the link just wrote and fails on
# any cycle of trivial forwarders, which makes the class self-announcing at build
# time instead of as a crash in front of a player. Lane FACEFIX, run link100.
add_custom_command(TARGET walk_window POST_BUILD
    COMMAND python "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/facecycle_guard.py"
            "$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:walk_window>/walk_window.map"
            --allow "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/facecycle_allow.txt"
    VERBATIM
    COMMENT "facecycle_guard: no face forwards to another face")

# A HOSTED DS GLOBAL MUST BE AT LEAST AS BIG AS WHAT THE ROM WRITES THROUGH
# IT. This class has shipped five times (memory note
# sm64ds-port-undersized-globals): a DS global takes hal/auto_bss.cpp's
# generous `int name[8]` default, the ROM routine that owns it writes its full
# extent, and the write lands on whatever the linker put next. It never
# presents as a bug in the subsystem that owns the buffer -- data_0209d74c
# cleared 3808 bytes through hal_wipes[0]'s vtable pointer and faulted
# HUD::Behavior the first time Mario talked, and the fix for it carried a
# comment asking the next person to re-run the audit after adding a symbol.
# Nobody did, the file grew from 152 symbols to 205, and on 2026-09-15 the
# re-audit found two more live instances seventy lines above that comment.
# A comment asking a human to remember is not a control, so this is the
# control: the check runs on every link instead of when somebody remembers.
# It reads only checked-in sources and config/arm9, so it needs no map, and
# it self-validates against seven fixtures on every run -- three that must
# fire and four that must not -- and fails the build if any of them comes
# back with the wrong verdict, so deleting or weakening a rule breaks the
# build rather than silently disarming the check. Lane BSSFIX, run link100.
add_custom_command(TARGET walk_window POST_BUILD
    COMMAND python "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/arm9_globals_guard.py"
            --root "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/.."
            --allow "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/arm9_globals_allow.txt"
    VERBATIM
    COMMENT "arm9_globals_guard: no ROM write runs past a hosted arm9 global")

    # .cpp) stores absolute pointers into the exe image -- every actor's
    # vtable pointer -- and they only relocate if the image loads at the
    # SAME base on the next launch. ASLR rebases once per boot, which
    # would refuse every state written before a reboot. The header still
    # checks the base, so if anything rebases the exe anyway the state is
    # refused with a message rather than loaded onto dangling pointers.
    target_link_options(walk_window_hires PRIVATE /DYNAMICBASE:NO)
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE ABI DEFECT DETECTORS
#
# port/tools/run_checks.py fires the receiver / calling-convention / vtable
# shape detectors and fails on any red, and on any VACUOUS pass (a checker
# that parsed nothing must not read as green):
#
#   aliascheck            an /alternatename that crosses the receiver boundary
#   vtspan --sweep        a host vtable array shorter than its ROM span
#   vtspan --fills        a fill loop that leaves a ROM slot unwritten
#   aritycheck            a declaration and a definition of one extern "C"
#                         symbol that disagree about how many parameters it
#                         takes (census, plus ratchets on the receiver shape
#                         and the plain-name func_* shape)
#   abicheck              a vtable thunk whose emitted `ret` breaks its slot's
#                         frame contract (needs this build's hal objects)
#
# TWO TARGETS, AND NEITHER IS IN ALL. That is deliberate. The port has no CI,
# so a target wired into ALL is the only thing that would run these for other
# people -- and turning a currently-green build red for every contributor is a
# decision for the port's owner, not for the lane that recovered the tools.
# Both are one command away:
#
#   ninja -C build/port port_checks_nobuild    the four no-build checkers
#   ninja -C build/port port_checks            + abicheck over THIS build
#
# port_checks_nobuild depends on nothing, so it runs even when the port does
# not fully link. port_checks depends on smoke_actor (which compiles
# actor_vtables.cpp and the other vtable-fill HAL objects), disassembles the
# build's hal objects with /disasm:nobytes, and runs the whole gate.
#
# THE DISASSEMBLY GOES IN THE BUILD DIRECTORY, never a fixed absolute path.
# The recovered wiring wrote to a shared C:/tmp/sm64ds-abisweep/_disasm, so
# two lanes running the suite at once would have written each other's input
# and each measured the other's build -- green, and meaningless.
find_program(PORT_PYTHON NAMES python python3 py)
if(PORT_PYTHON)
    add_custom_target(port_checks_nobuild
        COMMAND "${PORT_PYTHON}" "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/run_checks.py"
                "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}"
        WORKING_DIRECTORY "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}"
        COMMENT "port ABI checks (no build): aliascheck + vtspan + aritycheck"
        USES_TERMINAL VERBATIM)

    add_custom_target(port_abi_prove
        COMMAND "${PORT_PYTHON}" "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/abi_prove.py"
                "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}"
                --disasm-dir "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/_abicheck_disasm"
        WORKING_DIRECTORY "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}"
        COMMENT "prove each ABI checker green here and red on a re-broken copy"
        USES_TERMINAL VERBATIM)

    if(MSVC)
        # gen_disasm.cmd emits ONLY /disasm:nobytes. Plain /disasm makes
        # abicheck parse zero stores; abicheck refuses a zero-fill run and
        # run_checks refuses it again, but generating the wrong format is the
        # mistake that causes it, so the generator never produces anything
        # else.
        add_custom_target(port_checks
            COMMAND "${CMAKE_COMMAND}" -E echo
                    "== generating /disasm:nobytes for abicheck =="
            COMMAND cmd /c "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/gen_disasm.cmd"
                    "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}" "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/_abicheck_disasm"
            COMMAND "${PORT_PYTHON}"
                    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/run_checks.py"
                    "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}"
                    --disasm-dir "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/_abicheck_disasm"
            DEPENDS smoke_actor
            WORKING_DIRECTORY "${PORT_REPO_ROOT_ABS}"
            COMMENT "port ABI checks (full): + abicheck over this build"
            USES_TERMINAL VERBATIM)
    endif()
else()
    message(WARNING "python not found: the port ABI check targets were not "
                    "created")
endif()

# THE EXE'S OWN VERSION STRING, FOR THE CODE THAT HAS TO SAY IT.
#
# The performance log's header line names the game's version, and a report
# whose version came from a second copy of the number is a report that will one
# day name the wrong one. res/walk_window.rc below already holds the release
# version, is already bumped by hand per release, and is already the number a
# player sees in the exe's file properties -- so it is the one source, and this
# block lifts its ProductVersion string out at configure time into a
# compile-time define. Nothing to keep in step, and a release that bumps the
# resource bumps the report with it.
#
# The rc file joins the configure-time inputs so editing it reconfigures by
# itself (see "THE CONFIGURE-TIME INPUTS, REGISTERED" above); without that the
# define would keep the previous release's number until something else forced a
# configure.
set(PORT_GAME_VERSION "")
file(STRINGS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/res/walk_window.rc"
     PORT_RC_PRODUCTVERSION_LINES REGEX "VALUE[ \t]+\"ProductVersion\"")
foreach(rcline IN LISTS PORT_RC_PRODUCTVERSION_LINES)
    if(rcline MATCHES "\"ProductVersion\"[ \t]*,[ \t]*\"([0-9][0-9.]*)\"")
        set(PORT_GAME_VERSION "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
    endif()
endforeach()
if(PORT_GAME_VERSION STREQUAL "")
    message(WARNING "res/walk_window.rc has no readable ProductVersion: the "
                    "performance report's gameVersion will be empty")
endif()
set_property(DIRECTORY APPEND PROPERTY CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
             "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/res/walk_window.rc")
target_compile_definitions(walk_window PRIVATE
    PORT_GAME_VERSION="${PORT_GAME_VERSION}")
target_compile_definitions(walk_window_hires PRIVATE
    PORT_GAME_VERSION="${PORT_GAME_VERSION}")

# Windows identity resources: version info + icon for the game-shaped exes a
# player can meet (the bundle ships walk_window; hires is its sibling build of
# the same sources). Resources land in .rsrc and move nothing in .text, so the
# map-reading guards are untouched. The smokes stay bare on purpose: they are
# dev tools, not shipped artifacts. Version numbers live in res/walk_window.rc
# and are bumped by the release lane next to version.json.
if(WIN32)
    enable_language(RC)
    target_sources(walk_window PRIVATE res/walk_window.rc)
    target_sources(walk_window_hires PRIVATE res/walk_window.rc)
endif()

# ---- gate 2thr: THE RETIRED HOST PAIR, KEPT ONLY WHERE IT IS MEASURED ------
# run link2, lane THR.
#
# hal/os_thread.cpp's OS_SleepThread / OS_WakeupThread now compile only under
# PORT_OS_THREAD_HOST_PAIR, and these are the two targets that define it. Both
# are console probes with no window and no BMP, and mp_sleepwake's whole reason
# to exist is the A/B: ARM 1 links the ROM bodies with the manager globals
# stubbed at zero and MEASURES the 0xC0000005, ARM 2 links the host pair. Give
# ARM 2 the ROM bodies instead and the comparison it was written to make stops
# existing, so the retired stand-in stays reachable HERE and nowhere else.
#
# It is not reachable in a shipped target: walk_window, walk_window_hires and
# smoke_player take SLICE_COMMS_SOURCES, which now carries src/OS_SleepThread.c
# and src/OS_WakeupThread.c themselves. Neither probe links hal/cxx_aliases.cpp,
# so the ROM bodies could not link into them anyway -- the thread manager BSS
# they read (data_020a612c, data_020a6134, data_020a6128) lives there.
#
# WHAT THIS OWES: mp_sleepwake's ARM 2 half now describes a stand-in that no
# shipped binary carries. The probe still builds and still runs; its prose is a
# lane behind. port/tests/mp_sleepwake.cpp is not this lane's file.

target_compile_definitions(mp_comms_seam PRIVATE PORT_OS_THREAD_HOST_PAIR)

# GATE 221 (run link100, lane DF40): three host stand-ins retired out of the
# func_0203df40 / func_0203ea5c census -- the VS carousel's poll
# (hal/scene_vs_menu.cpp's VS_SEAM block) and the WM status-word
# read-modify-write pair (hal/comms_seam.cpp's g_wm_status). The whole census,
# including why the other 299 rows of those two closures are NOT work, is in
# port/slice_gate221.txt's own header.
#
# ON ALL THREE BIG TARGETS, and not by preference. Each retired host body lived
# in a file every one of them compiles -- hal/comms_seam.cpp rides
# SLICE_COMMS_SOURCES and hal/scene_vs_menu.cpp rides SLICE_VS_SOURCES, and both
# variables go to exactly walk_window, walk_window_hires and smoke_player. A
# target that lost the face without gaining the body would fail at link, so the
# three move together. Appended as target_sources ABOVE the sharing block below,
# which reads the three targets' SOURCES back off them: a source on all three
# joins the single shared compile by itself.
#
# mp_comms_seam also links hal/comms_seam.cpp directly and does NOT get these
# rows. It does not need them: nothing that probe links references
# func_02040a5c or func_02040a84 (only src/func_0203ea5c.c and the wide copy do,
# and neither is in it), so the two names are simply never referenced there.
port_read_lines("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/slice_gate221.txt" SLICE221_LINES)
set(SLICE221_SOURCES "")

# which is what src/_ZN3IRQ13DmaTimHandlerEj.cpp defines. ONE ADDRESS, TWO
# NAMES -- the gate-216 rename block's case, and it takes gate 224's answer: a

#
# GATE 225b: THE THREE SIBLING FADER TABLES' DESTRUCTOR PAIR. gate 219 above
# seated all ten slots of data_0208eacc / data_0208eb2c and both function words

# re-seating needs "the same kind of dispatch-site audit port/fader_boot_map.txt
# section 9c did for data_0208ea6c, extended to data_0209f5bc / data_0209d4ac's
# OTHER readers". That audit was done: every reader of those two pointers in
# arm9 and all 101 overlay reloc files was resolved to its owning function and
# each owner's src TU read for the slot index it dispatches. Forty functions
# read the pointers and they dispatch slots 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8. SLOTS 0, 1

# GATE SLOT5 -- the thirty Render bodies the destructor fold kept unlinked
# ===========================================================================
#
# mwccarm spends TWO vtable entries on `virtual ~X()` (the Itanium D1/D0 pair)
# and MSVC folds them into one, so every virtual declared after the destructor
# sat one slot early on the host through the whole model hierarchy. The ROM's
# _ZTV9ModelAnim spends slot 5 on Render; the folded host table spent it on
# Virtual18, which takes an argument more. Thirty matched Render bodies that
# dispatch that slot through a local six-virtual shadow were therefore dropped
# from their own gates' slices and hand-transcribed into
# unmatched/ModelAnim_Renders.cpp and unmatched/BobEnemy_Renders.cpp.
#
# include/ModelBase.h and its six siblings now spell the destructor pair as two
# plain virtuals under _MSC_VER, so the host numbers the table the ROM's way
# and the hand copies have nothing left to work around. slice_slot5.txt carries
# the thirty sources, each verified against the word at its class vtable's
# slot 9 in config/arm9/overlays/<ov>/relocs.txt before it was enrolled.
#
# THE FACES ARE THE OTHER HALF. Every one of the thirty fill sites declares the
# Itanium name at C linkage and calls it, because the host copy it reached was
# an extern "C" definition; the matched sources define __thiscall methods, and
# no linker alias bridges ecx against the stack. hal/cxxname_bridge.cpp carries
# the thirty one-line faces, so no fill site changes.

# ===========================================================================
# R10a, run link100 lane PMFB2: THE SEATED-TABLE ROWS
# ===========================================================================
#
# Rows that were host-copied only because the DATA under them held a DS code
# word, taken off their host copies once a boot-time installer puts a host
# address there. Nothing in this block changes a ROM reference, a linker
# option or a call the ROM does not make; the per-row derivation, the ROM
# stride and the emitted stride are in port/slice_pmfb2.txt.
#
# THE /Zp4 IS LANE PMFB1's BLOCK R9d LEVER, CARRIED. PMFB1 found that MSVC
# gives any struct CONTAINING a pointer-to-member an alignment of eight, which
# rounded eleven twenty-byte ROM records up to twenty-four and would have made
# every state after state 0 read the wrong record, silently. Every TU listed
# here had its ROM stride re-derived out of the overlay image and its emitted
# stride read off a /FAsc listing for THIS lane, and the option is on the set
# whether or not it moves that TU today, so that a later header edit cannot
# reintroduce the defect without the measurement being redone.
#
# WHICH TUs IN THIS BLOCK THE OPTION ACTUALLY MOVES, measured one at a time:
#   src/_ZN16dPathLiftActor_c12BaseBehaviorEv.cpp   24 -> 20, and the ROM strides 20.
#       Its record is {char pad[8]; PLFn fn; char tail[4]} -- a struct that
#       CONTAINS a pointer-to-member, which is PMFB1's exact case.
#   the two ov006 rows                     8 either way; their record is two
#       plain ints, so the listings are identical but for the TITLE line.
# The other three batch-3 rows are NOT on this list at all: their tables are
# arrays of the bare pointer-to-member, which is eight bytes with or without
# the option, and adding it would be a claim nothing measured.
# lane CDEFS 2026-09-16: dScMgSound_c.cpp was listed here AND in a later
# set_source_files_properties() for COMPILE_OPTIONS. That later call REPLACES
# this one (the property is set, not appended), so this row never reached
# the compiler for that TU. Removed from this row only; the other sources
# in the row keep it, and the surviving row for dScMgSound_c.cpp is unchanged.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/_ZN16dPathLiftActor_c12BaseBehaviorEv.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "/Zp4")
# dScMgSound_c.cpp also carries a fall-off-the-end body (dScMgSound_c::Virtual50),
# so it takes /wd4716 as well -- in THIS row, because COMPILE_OPTIONS is one
# property and a second set_source_files_properties would drop the /Zp4 above.
# The block at the end of this file explains the option.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/actors/dScMgSound_c.cpp"
    # and the generated copy, lane DUPES: this TU is on PORT_HOSTGEN_TU
    # now, so the raw path alone would set the property on a source
    # nothing compiles.
    "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src/src/actors/dScMgSound_c.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "/Zp4;/wd4716")
# src/func_ov002_020aea30.cpp is a //cpp-marked .c: its own text spells
# `typedef void (C::*PMF)(int, int);`, which is not C. The tree's standing
# treatment for that is LANGUAGE CXX on the source, and this is one more of
# them.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/func_ov002_020aea30.cpp"
    PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CXX)
port_read_lines("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/slice_pmfb2.txt" SLICE_PMFB2_LINES)
set(SLICE_PMFB2_SOURCES "")
foreach(line IN LISTS SLICE_PMFB2_LINES)
    string(STRIP "${line}" line)
    if(line MATCHES "^#" OR line STREQUAL "")
        continue()
    endif()
    list(APPEND SLICE_PMFB2_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../${line}")
endforeach()
foreach(_tpmfb2 walk_window walk_window_hires smoke_player)
    target_sources(${_tpmfb2} PRIVATE ${SLICE_PMFB2_SOURCES})
endforeach()

# ===========================================================================
# R10d, run link100 lane MGWRITER: THE OBJECT-FIELD ROWS AND THEIR WRITER
# ===========================================================================
#
# Blocks R10a, R10b and R10c took rows that read a TABLE. This block takes rows
# that read an OBJECT FIELD: there is no table for a boot installer to verify
# and rewrite, so what the installer seats is the SOURCE the writer copies from,
# and the field carries a host word from the moment the writer runs. Four of the
# six rows lane PMFB3 measured and left, plus the writer that fills two of the
# fields, come off their host copies here. Nothing in this block changes a ROM
# reference, a linker option or a call the ROM does not make; the per-row ROM
# disassembly, emitted dispatch shape, source pairs, sweep and alias spelling
# are in port/slice_mgwriter.txt and the raw measurements in
# runs/link100/out/MGWRITER/.
#
# NO /Zp4 ON THIS BLOCK, measured per TU rather than inherited. R10a carries
# lane PMFB1's lever because MSVC gives any struct CONTAINING a pointer to
# member eight-byte alignment, which silently strides twenty-four where the ROM
# strides twenty. Four of these five TUs hold the pointer to member as a FIELD
# rather than in a table, and the fifth reads an array of the bare pointer to
# member; every one was compiled under the port's own flags with and without the
# option for this lane and each pair of /FAsc listings came back identical
# except for the TITLE line naming the .obj. R10a's rule for that case is to
# leave the option off rather than make a claim nothing measured.
#
# WHAT MAKES THE FOUR FIELD ROWS COMPILE AT ALL is block R8's /vmg /vmm on the
# whole target: their src structs put a state word after a pointer to member and
# the ROM reads it at +0x20, which is only true at the ROM's own eight-byte
# member pointer. The four emitted field offsets (+0x0c, +0x04, +0x14, +0x0c)
# agree with the ROM's own word for word, so the structs are right and the old
# note in unmatched/MgBase_StateDispatch.cpp about a four-byte member pointer
# moving every later field is a premise that expired when R8 landed.
port_read_lines("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/slice_mgwriter.txt" SLICE_MGWRITER_LINES)

        continue()
    endif()
    list(APPEND SLICE_MGWRITER_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../${line}")

# the reason R10a and R10c both give: MSVC gives any struct CONTAINING a pointer
# to member eight-byte alignment, which silently strides twenty-four where the
# ROM strides twenty. Every TU in this block was compiled under the port's own
# flags with and without the option for this lane, and each pair of /FAsc
# listings came back identical except for the TITLE line naming the .obj --
# these tables are arrays of the bare pointer to member or of a one-member Entry
# wrapping one, eight bytes either way, against the ROM's own
# `add r3, rTable, rIndex, lsl #3`. R10a's rule for that case is to leave the
# option off rather than make a claim nothing measured.
port_read_lines("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/slice_pmfb5.txt" SLICE_PMFB5_LINES)
set(SLICE_PMFB5_SOURCES "")
foreach(line IN LISTS SLICE_PMFB5_LINES)
    string(STRIP "${line}" line)
    if(line MATCHES "^#" OR line STREQUAL "")
        continue()
    endif()
    list(APPEND SLICE_PMFB5_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../${line}")
endforeach()
foreach(_tpmfb5 walk_window walk_window_hires smoke_player)
    target_sources(${_tpmfb5} PRIVATE ${SLICE_PMFB5_SOURCES})

# ===========================================================================
# R10e, run link100 lane FWD: THE MEMBER-DEFINING Behavior ROWS
# ===========================================================================
#
# Blocks R10a through R10d took rows whose matched TU defines the FLAT C symbol
# the port's face calls. This block takes the nine that do not: their matched
# TU defines a real C++ MEMBER (`int BowserFire::Behavior()`), which MSVC
# decorates ?Behavior@BowserFire@@QAEHXZ and calls __thiscall, while the port's
# actor-class face calls the flat name with the receiver on the stack. Two
# symbols, two conventions; an /alternatename cannot bridge them and lane PMFB5
# paid a link to establish it. The bridge is port/hal/fwd_forwarders.cpp, one
# forwarder per class in the flat name's own convention, and it rides this
# block's slice file so the forwarders and the TUs they reach land together.
# Nothing here changes a ROM reference, a linker option or a call the ROM does
# not make. The per-row ROM stride, emitted stride, arity, source pairs, config
# span and alias spelling are in port/slice_fwd.txt and the raw measurements in
# runs/link100/out/FWD/.
#
# NO /Zp4 ON THIS BLOCK, measured per TU rather than inherited, for the reason
# R10a, R10c and R10d all give. Every one of these nine TUs was compiled under
# the port's own flags with and without the option for this lane and each pair
# of /FAsc listings came back identical outside the TITLE line naming the .obj.
# R10a's rule for that case is to leave the option off rather than make a claim
# nothing measured.
# GATE 2. src/_ZN12MetalNetLift8BehaviorEv.cpp is a //cpp-marked .c whose own text spells
# `typedef void (C::*PMF)();`, which is not C. The tree's standing treatment for
# that is LANGUAGE CXX on the source (lane PMFB2 did it for
# src/func_ov002_020aea30.cpp), and this is one more of them.

# GATE 3. /Zp4 ON ONE SOURCE, MEASURED AND NOT INHERITED.
# src/actors/dMgJump3DMario_c.cpp spells `struct C { char pad[0x3c]; PMF m; };` and
# the ROM's field is at +0x3c. MSVC aligns an eight-byte member to eight, so
# without /Zp4 the TU reads [edi+64] and [edi+68] -- FOUR BYTES LATE -- and with
# it the same listing reads [edi+60] and [edi+64], the ROM's own offsets. Those
# two instructions are the ONLY difference between the two /FAsc listings
# (runs/link100/out/PMFB6/emit_gate3_out.txt). The other two gate-3 rows were
# compiled both ways and their listings are identical outside the TITLE, so the
# option is claimed on this ONE source and on nothing else -- the treatment lane
# MGWRITER named for func_ov006_020c07e8, measured here rather than inherited.
#
# BOTH PATHS, run link100 lane HOSTGEN4: this TU joined PORT_HOSTGEN_TU for its
# nine decorated ROM data rows, so the compile the build actually runs is the
# generated copy under build/port/host-src. /Zp4 is the pack that puts the PMF
# at the ROM's +0x3c; naming only the src/ row would leave the generated copy
# reading four bytes late, which is the exact drift the check near line 380
# refuses. The src/ row is kept so the property is still right if the
# substitution is ever retired.
set_source_files_properties(
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/actors/dMgJump3DMario_c.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/host-src/src/actors/dMgJump3DMario_c.cpp"
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "/Zp4")

    target_sources(${_tpmfb6} PRIVATE ${SLICE_PMFB6_SOURCES})
endforeach()
